components.name: clinical_indication
components.label: HAS_CLINICAL_INDICATION
components.description: Use this edge to read the release's clinical-development roll-up for a drug-disease pair.

properties.name: maxClinicalStage
properties.description: Use this value as the pair's maximum clinical stage.

components.name: clinical_precedence_evidence
components.label: CLINICAL_PRECEDENCE_EVIDENCE
components.description: Read target -> disease for clinical-precedence evidence.

properties.name: clinicalReportId
properties.description: The report the row was built from, in the same mixed id shapes as clinical_report.id; resolved by equality only.

properties.name: clinicalStage
properties.description: The report's own harmonised stage, not a pair-level maximum; all 13 codes occur, WITHDRAWAL and PHASE_4 included.

properties.name: drugId
properties.description: The ChEMBL molecule id of the drug the report names; all non-null values resolve in drug_molecule.id.

properties.name: drugFromSource
properties.description: The drug name as the source wrote it, with case and leading spaces unnormalised.

properties.name: trialWhyStopped
properties.description: The registry's free-text stop reason, verbatim; null on labels, approvals and warnings rather than on a stopped trial with a lost reason.

properties.name: trialStopReasonCategories
properties.description: Classifier labels read from the stop reason, in PascalCase codes; a null list means the report is not a stopped trial.

properties.name: studyStartDate
properties.description: The report's study start date as source text; null for labels, approvals and warnings.

properties.name: evidenceDate
properties.description: The earlier of publicationDate and studyStartDate as source text: the first date at which the evidence existed.

properties.name: publicationDate
properties.description: The oldest publication date among the cited literature, as source text; not the report's own date.

properties.name: literature
properties.description: PubMed ids the report cites, as strings; a null list means the report cites nothing.

properties.name: score
properties.description: The stage's rank value, halved once when Negative or Safety_Sideeffects is present; 14 discrete values from 0.005 to 1.0 and not comparable with another source's score.

properties.name: directionOnTrait
properties.description: Always 'protect'; an assumption of therapeutic intent emitted with every disease id, not a measured direction.

properties.name: directionOnTarget
properties.description: LoF or GoF translated from the drug's mechanism action type; null when the action type falls outside both lists, and the same value on every target row of the drug.

components.name: clinical_target
components.label: HAS_CLINICAL_TARGET
components.description: Use this edge to read the release's drug-target pair with clinical reports naming the drug.

properties.name: maxClinicalStage
properties.description: Use this value as the drug's maximum clinical stage.

components.name: clinical_trial_has_side_effect
components.label: HAS_SIDE_EFFECT
components.description: Use this edge to read the adverse-event term a warning report names as a side effect.

properties.name: termFromSource
properties.description: The side-effect label the warning source wrote: the term's own label or, failing that, its warning class.

components.name: clinical_trial_published_in
components.label: PUBLISHED_IN
components.description: Use this edge to read the publication a report cites.

properties.name: referenceType
properties.description: The registry's role for the reference: BACKGROUND, DERIVED or RESULT.

components.name: clinical_trial_studies_disease
components.label: STUDIES_DISEASE
components.description: Use this edge to read the disease a report studied, approved, withdrew or warned against.

components.name: clinical_trial_studies_molecule
components.label: STUDIES_MOLECULE
components.description: Use this edge to read the molecule a report studies, labels or warns about.

components.name: credible_set_colocalises_with
components.label: COLOCALISES_WITH
components.description: Use this edge to read a colocalisation the release reports between two credible sets.

properties.name: colocalisationMethod
properties.description: Use this value to identify the method that produced the colocalisation.

properties.name: clpp
properties.description: Use this value as the colocalisation posterior probability for the pair.

properties.name: h3
properties.description: Read h3 against h4: h3 high with h4 low argues against a shared variant.

properties.name: h4
properties.description: Use this value with h3 to read the hypothesis that the two sets share one causal variant.

properties.name: betaRatioSignAverage
properties.description: Use this value to read whether the two studies' effects point the same way.

properties.name: numberColocalisingVariants
properties.description: Use this value as the number of variants in the shared signal.

properties.name: chromosome
properties.description: Use this value as the colocalising locus's chromosome.

properties.name: rightStudyType
properties.description: Use this value as the right credible set's study type.

components.name: credible_set_contains_variant
components.label: CONTAINS_VARIANT
components.description: Use this edge to read a variant's membership in a fine-mapped credible set.

properties.name: posteriorProbability
properties.description: Use this value as the variant's membership probability in the set.

properties.name: logBF
properties.description: Use this value as the variant's log Bayes factor for set membership.

properties.name: beta
properties.description: Use this value with the study and credible set to read the variant's effect estimate.

properties.name: standardError
properties.description: Use this value with beta.

properties.name: pValueMantissa
properties.description: Read this value with pValueExponent.

properties.name: pValueExponent
properties.description: Use this value only with pValueMantissa.

properties.name: r2Overall
properties.description: Use this value as the variant's LD to the set's lead variant.

components.label: HAS_LEAD_VARIANT
components.description: Use this edge to read each credible set's lead variant.

properties.description: The sponsor's registry class: INDUSTRY, NIH, OTHER_GOV, NETWORK, FED, INDIV or OTHER.

properties.name: phaseFromSource
properties.description: The stage string exactly as the source stated it, before harmonisation (for example PHASE2, phase 1/phase 2, withdrawn, black box warning).

properties.name: trialPhase
properties.description: The registry's own phase code (PHASE1, PHASE1/PHASE2, PHASE2/PHASE3, PHASE4, EARLY_PHASE1); null on non-registry rows and where the registry recorded none.

properties.name: trialOverallStatus
properties.description: The registry's recruitment and availability status (COMPLETED, TERMINATED, RECRUITING, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, UNKNOWN, ...); not a study result.

properties.name: trialWhyStopped
properties.description: The sponsor's free-text reason for ending the study.

properties.name: trialStopReasonCategories
properties.description: Classifier labels assigned to a stopped study, up to three per row; Uncategorised is the classifier's fallback, not a sponsor's reason.

properties.name: countries
properties.description: The markets a drug warning was issued in, split from the warning's own semicolon string; filled on the 2,744 SAFETY rows only and as free text with no country code scheme.

properties.name: trialDescription
properties.description: The registry's brief summary of the study, as free text.

properties.name: trialOfficialTitle
properties.description: The registered title as the sponsor wrote it.

properties.name: title
properties.description: The report heading: the registered title when one exists, otherwise a sentence the build generated from the stage, first drug and first disease.

properties.name: trialPrimaryPurpose
properties.description: The registry's declared primary purpose (TREATMENT, PREVENTION, BASIC_SCIENCE, DIAGNOSTIC, ...); null is not the OTHER code.

properties.name: trialStudyType
properties.description: The registry's design class, kept to three values: INTERVENTIONAL, OBSERVATIONAL or EXPANDED_ACCESS.

properties.name: trialNumberOfArms
properties.description: The number of arms the registry recorded; a null is not zero arms.

properties.name: trialStartDate
properties.description: The date the study began; 1900-01-31 and 2099-01-01 are registry placeholders, not measured starts.

properties.name: year
properties.description: The year a drug warning was issued; filled on warning rows only and not the year of a trial or an approval.

properties.name: url
properties.description: The source record's address; not a key, because one source document can back several reports.

properties.name: qualityControls
properties.description: Flags naming a reason a consumer may drop the report (NO_DISEASE, UNVALIDATED_INDICATION, INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE, PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED, SAFETY_REPORT); flagged rows stay published.

purpose.text: Target-disease evidence review and prioritisation over the Open Targets 26.09 release. For one target, disease or other entity, a consumer asks which relations the release reports, what each relation means and where it came from, and may compare those relations using the release's own scores.

limitations.text: Do not read the graph as what an upstream authority permits or what an earlier release contained, and do not read a relation as implying more than the release reports.

Do not read an association as a statistical association in a study, a causal relation or claim, or a prediction made by this graph; do not read the graph as target validation or establishing causation.
Do not read evidence as one harmonised quantity comparable across evidence sources; do not read a score as comparable across datasets unless the graph states the comparison.
Do not read an identifier as the Platform resolver, which normalises the separator on lookup; a join, filter or resolver must use the form the column actually carries.
Do not read a score as a probability, a p-value, or one universal confidence measure.

claims.text: A knowledge graph of the Open Targets Platform 26.09 release. Nodes are entities the release identifies; edges are relations the release reports, derives or lets a consumer read from its records. The graph is a semantic index over the release, not a replacement for the release's own data.
The graph describes what the 26.09 files were measured to contain.
A target-disease relation reported by the release from one or more evidence sources, with a score and evidence count.
A source-specific observation that a target is linked to a disease or phenotype; the observation carries the source's own method and score.
The spelling of an ontology accession in the release: PREFIX_accession and PREFIX:accession are different strings.
A source-specific numeric judgement; different datasets call different statistics score.
Ensembl gene identifiers (ENSG) are stable human gene accessions.
Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO), MONDO, HPO, GO, SO and Reactome accessions denote ontology terms in their respective namespaces.
A target-disease association score is a weighted aggregate over evidence sources; its scale and weighting are release-specific.

The parents and children arrays are not exact inverses in this release: 6,907 parent edges have no reverse child entry and 963 child entries no reverse parent, so a down-walk and an up-walk disagree.
child biosampleId and parent biosampleId joined by '|': 64,085 edges over 32,752 child terms, with unique pairs.

Direct parents only; a row has several parents when the class belongs to several ontology branches. 2,725 rows carry a null parents array, which does not distinguish an ontology root from a class whose parents the build dropped. 109 parent elements (19 distinct ids) name no biosample row and land on no node. 617 parent elements are full URLs, and parents cross ontology prefixes.

purpose.text: The biosample relation fulfils the IS_A use as the step from a biosample to its direct ontology parents: each relation row supplies an edge for each parent it lists, keyed by the child and parent ids, covering the direct parents the release writes. The edge runs child to parent only and publishes direct parents rather than the source's precomputed closures, so an ancestor walk must traverse it recursively and a parent the vocabulary lacks still leaves an edge on no node.

limitations.text: No edge means this source reports no direct aggregate for the pair. It does not mean the source measured the pair and found nothing, and it does not mean the pair is unassociated; another source may still carry it. The release emits no placeholder row; the only 0.0 scores are the 57 rows whose evidenceCount is null.

This score is not the overall direct score and is not comparable with it: the overall score is the weighted cross-source fold, while this row carries the source's own fold without that weighting. Per-source scores are therefore not shares and do not sum to the overall. The timeseries is not carried on the edge.
Do not read the value in aggregationValue as a numeric score or an ordering.
Adding or averaging a pair's per-source scores does not reproduce its overall direct score, and a higher per-source score from one source does not mean a stronger finding than another source's row.
Do not read the per-source rows as shares of one score that can be summed.
Each source folds its own evidence units, so a europepmc score and a crispr score on the same pair are not comparable findings.

The weights are release-frozen and differ by source: on a single-source pair the overall is a fixed 0.1217, 0.3041 or 0.6083 times this score.

purpose.text: Use it to walk a pathway's direct parents and children.

limitations.text: ancestors, descendants and path stay in reactome and are not edges. ancestors and descendants are transitive closures that repeat what this walk already gives; path is an ordered route (up to 11 per row, 75 rows with more than one root) whose canonical order is a build choice, not a relation. To get ancestry, walk this edge. Pathway membership is not a target-disease assertion.

claims.text: The child pathway is part of the direct parent pathway.
child reactome.id and parent reactome.id joined by '|': 2,899 edges with 2,899 distinct pairs.
2,854 pathways have at least one parent, 29 are roots, and a pathway has up to 6 parents. The parents and children arrays are exact inverses here: every parent element has its reverse child element.

purpose.text: The reactome relation fulfils the IS_PART_OF use as the direct containment link between a pathway and each parent it lists: each release row is the child and contributes one edge per parent, keyed by the two accessions, and every parent resolves to a pathway. It supplies direct child-to-parent links only; ancestors and descendants are closures this walk reproduces, path stays an ordered route in the source, and a root pathway carries no parent edge.

limitations.text: An empty parents array emits no edge: the 29 pathways that are release roots carry none, and the binding adds no parent for them.
The binding emits child -> parent only and reads no children array, so a parent-to-child walk must traverse IS_PART_OF in reverse.

claims.text: One PathwayIsPartOfEdge per element of reactome.parents.
child reactome.id|parent reactome.id: 2,899 edges with 2,899 distinct pairs.
The row is the child and the array element the direct parent; a pathway with up to six parents yields one edge per parent.
Every parent key names a reactome row, so no edge of this set dangles.

A drug the annotation concerns, one edge per element of the row's drugs array. A multi-drug annotation keeps one row and therefore several edges.

(pmid, keywordType, keywordId). literature_entity_lut is unique on (pmid, keywordId) — 173,137,629 rows and no duplicate pair in 26.09 — and every keywordId belongs to one keywordType, so the triple is the row identity. Edges are keyed pmid::<class>::keywordId.

purpose.text: Use this value to rank mentions within their own paper.

purpose.text: The evidence_uniprot_literature relation fulfils the EVIDENCE_UNIPROT_LITERATURE use as the record of one target-disease link that UniProt curated from the literature: each relation row is one node, keyed by the release's evidence id, and the relation covers the associations the source curates. The binding copies the evidence envelope plus publicationDate, diseaseFromSource, diseaseFromSourceId, confidence and targetModulation; an envelope column this source lacks is bound as null.
publicationDate is null on 62 rows.
The source's 26,342 PMID elements are mapped by the separate supported_by binding.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's pharmacogenomic clinical annotation.

limitations.text: A null is not a uniform absence: the nulls are source gaps with different causes.

studyId is ClinPGx's annotation accession and joins to no row of the release's study dataset: the shared name is a collision. genotypeId is a genotype spelling (chr_pos_ref_allele1,allele2), not a variant id, and one genotype can name two variants. variantAnnotation stays in the source: it holds the per-publication variant statements and is not a graph relation here. genotypeAnnotationText is ClinPGx's sentence for the genotype; phenotypeText is the release's phrase cut from it, so it is neither always the source sentence nor a ClinPGx term, and never a controlled vocabulary. An annotation grades evidence; it is not a prescription, a dose recommendation or a clinical guideline.
The number of PGX_ANNOTATION nodes is neither the number of ClinPGx clinical annotations nor the number of variant annotations; one annotation fans out over genotypes, phenotypes and drugs.
A level-1A annotation is not a clinical guideline recommendation, and a level-3 annotation is not an unscored record; level 3 is the modal low-evidence bucket.
A null phenotypeFromSourceId does not mean the annotation states no drug-response phenotype.

claims.text: pgxCategory is the curated role of the phenotype (toxicity, efficacy, metabolism/pk, dosage, other, pd). directionality is the allele-function label of the genotype, not the direction of the drug response. evidenceLevel is ClinPGx's grade of the annotation, on ClinPGx's scale, 1A highest and 4 meaning the evidence does not support the association. phenotypeText is the drug-response phrase, and phenotypeFromSourceId is a sparse mapped disease term: the disease accession the release mapped it to. isDirectTarget is build-computed: true when the gene is a mechanism-of-action target of a drug in the row. variantId is derived by the build from genotypeId, not supplied by ClinPGx.

One pharmacogenomic clinical annotation: a statement that a genotype or haplotype changes a drug's behaviour for one gene, curated under one phenotype category and graded by ClinPGx. It is the release's pharmacogenomics row, not a study, a variant or a drug label.

studyId|genotype|variantId|variantFunctionalConsequenceId|targetFromSourceId|pgxCategory|phenotypeText|phenotypeFromSourceId|drug set: 33,479 nodes for 33,479 rows. studyId alone is not the key: it is the ClinPGx clinical-annotation accession with 5,190 distinct values and up to 270 rows each, because one annotation fans out over genotypes, phenotypes and drugs. All nine parts are needed: dropping studyId leaves 32,551 distinct keys, phenotypeText 29,503, the drug set 26,558, targetFromSourceId 24,997, genotype 23,929, pgxCategory 32,495, variantId 33,366, variantFunctionalConsequenceId 33,473 and phenotypeFromSourceId 33,471. The drug set is the sorted drugId|drugFromSource pairs of the row. genotypeId, variantRsId and haplotypeId do not discriminate further and stay properties.
The node is keyed by the annotation's subject plus its fan-out axes.

phenotypeFromSourceId is null on 32,755 rows (the label lookup matched nothing, although phenotypeText is still present on 31,625 of them), variantId on 17,310 (the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows plus 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes that reduce to the reference), variantRsId on 9,548, variantFunctionalConsequenceId on 11,117, directionality on 26,453, targetFromSourceId on 1,569, haplotypeId on 23,931 and phenotypeText on 1,130.
0 of the 5,190 studyId values occur in the release's study dataset.
variantAnnotation holds 47,749 elements, 1-80 per row and 10,288 distinct ids.
phenotypeText is the release's phrase cut from genotypeAnnotationText on 29,818 of the 32,349 non-null rows and different from it on 2,531.
