Do not read an association as a statistical association in a study, a causal relation or claim, or a prediction made by this graph; do not read the graph as target validation or establishing causation.
Do not read evidence as one harmonised quantity comparable across evidence sources; do not read a score as comparable across datasets unless the graph states the comparison.
Do not read an identifier as the Platform resolver, which normalises the separator on lookup; a join, filter or resolver must use the form the column actually carries.
Do not read a score as a probability, a p-value, or one universal confidence measure.

claims.text: A knowledge graph of the Open Targets Platform 26.09 release. Nodes are entities the release identifies; edges are relations the release reports, derives or lets a consumer read from its records. The graph is a semantic index over the release, not a replacement for the release's own data.
The graph describes what the 26.09 files were measured to contain.
A target-disease relation reported by the release from one or more evidence sources, with a score and evidence count.
A source-specific observation that a target is linked to a disease or phenotype; the observation carries the source's own method and score.
The spelling of an ontology accession in the release: PREFIX_accession and PREFIX:accession are different strings.
A source-specific numeric judgement; different datasets call different statistics score.
Ensembl gene identifiers (ENSG) are stable human gene accessions.
Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO), MONDO, HPO, GO, SO and Reactome accessions denote ontology terms in their respective namespaces.
A target-disease association score is a weighted aggregate over evidence sources; its scale and weighting are release-specific.

purpose.text: Use an entity node as the release's identified record of one thing a consumer can ask about.

limitations.text: No node means the release does not identify the entity in this build.
An edge between two entities records the relation the concrete edge declares; it does not make the entities interchangeable.

claims.text: An entity with its own identity in the release: a target, disease, molecule, variant, study, credible set or another identified record.
The concrete node's own release identifier.

purpose.text: Use the text as the term identity in this release because the code is empty.

limitations.text: The label is not normalised across MedDRA versions.

claims.text: The MedDRA preferred-term label for the adverse event.

purpose.text: Use it to query the source gap.

limitations.text: It identifies nothing and must not key a node.
Do not join MedDRA terms on this property in 26.09.

claims.text: The MedDRA code carried by the signal row; it is an empty string for all 118,247 rows in 26.09.
The field is present but valueless throughout this release.

purpose.text: Use an adverse event node to identify a MedDRA term in the release's drug-reaction signals.

limitations.text: An event absent here had no significant signal for any molecule in the release; it is not absent from MedDRA or from clinical practice.
The term is a MedDRA vocabulary item, not an Open Targets disease or phenotype id. It does not join DiseaseNode without a mapping the release does not supply.

claims.text: A MedDRA adverse event term used in the release's openFDA drug reaction signals.
The event text, keyed adverse_event::<event>. meddraCode is an empty string on every 26.09 row, so the code cannot identify the term; the event text is the only discriminating field.
event is the MedDRA preferred-term label. meddra_code is retained as a property and carries the release's empty string.

purpose.text: Use an ontology term node as the release's controlled-vocabulary entry when reading a term or its hierarchy.

limitations.text: An absent term is outside the release's ontology subset.
A term is vocabulary, not an assertion about any entity.

claims.text: An ontology term the release uses as a controlled vocabulary entry.
The concrete term's accession.

purpose.text: Use name as the biosample's display label; join on biosampleId.

limitations.text: Not a key: one name can stand for up to three classes. The column holds only the ontology's label, never a study's or datasource's own tissue wording.

claims.text: The class's label as the contributing ontology writes it.
Present on every row; 35,273 distinct names cover 35,477 rows. 710 values are URLs rather than readable anatomical text.

purpose.text: Read description for the contributing ontology's definition of the class.

limitations.text: A null description does not mark a class the Platform failed to annotate, and a non-null description is ontology prose, not a measured property of a sample.

claims.text: The class definition as the contributing ontology publishes it.
Null on 7,414 of 35,477 rows, which records that the contributing ontology publishes no definition for the class; its name and parents are intact.

purpose.text: Use a biosample node to identify and join the release's experimental contexts.

limitations.text: A biosample absent here is outside the release's vocabulary. A null description is the contributing ontology publishing no definition, not an absent class.

A tissue, a cell type and a cell line share this node type; the id prefix is not a kind discriminator, and parents cross ontology prefixes (anatomy classes have GO, CL and SO parents). The graph publishes the direct hierarchy only; cross-references stay in the source, so use the hierarchy and the id prefix, not the label, to tell kinds apart.

claims.text: A class in the release's merged biosample vocabulary: a tissue, cell type, cell line or another ontology class used to describe an experimental context.
biosample.biosampleId: 35,477 rows and 35,477 distinct ids, never null. 34,120 are PREFIX_accession CURIEs, 1,338 are full ontology URLs, and 19 are other OBO or bare forms such as uberon#LATIN.
biosampleName is a label; the id is the join key. Direct ontology parents are BiosampleIsAEdge; ancestors and descendants stay in the source as precomputed closures and are not published as edges.

purpose.text: Use name as the cell line's display label in plots and tooltips; it is not a stable identifier.

limitations.text: Never null in the screens; the build falls back to the CCLE name and then to a disease-derived label.
Not unique, because fallback labels merge distinct lines; group on depmapId instead.

claims.text: Display name of the cell line used in the screen.
A label for plots and tooltips, not a stable identifier.

purpose.text: Read tissue to group or display cell lines by the screen's lineage category.

limitations.text: The build substitutes 'other' for an unnamed lineage, so a value exists rather than a hole.
A lineage group pools many cell lines and diseases; it is not a biosample.

claims.text: Tissue or lineage category label of the screen group.
A curation-file label for a group of cell lines, not a measured tissue.

purpose.text: Use tissue_id to place the screen group in an ontology namespace.

limitations.text: Null when the lineage had no ontology match, which is the 'other' bucket.
Not biosample.biosampleId despite the release's declared join; it is an ontology term.

claims.text: Ontology accession for the tissue or lineage category of the screen group.
Mostly UBERON accessions in underscore form, with one CL accession, so the namespace matters.

purpose.text: Read disease as the cell line's source disease label for display and grouping.

limitations.text: Never null in the screens, because no disease mapping is applied.
It does not join disease.id; a dependency in a line labelled with a disease is not evidence about that disease.

claims.text: Primary disease the cell line was derived from, in DepMap's Oncotree vocabulary.
A source label, not a disease id; it includes Non-Cancerous.

purpose.text: Use a cell-line node to identify the DepMap model behind the release's essentiality screens.

limitations.text: A line absent here was not used by the release's essentiality screens; a CRISPR line is CRISPR_CELL_LINE, and other assays publish no line node.
A cell-line dependency is an in-vitro observation. It does not establish essentiality in a human tissue or a therapeutic window.

claims.text: A DepMap cell line named by the release's target-essentiality screens. It is the experimental model, not the tissue it came from.
The release's DepMap cell-line identifier; the build key is depmap_id and the name is a display label, not a fallback key. The same line can appear in several screens.
Tissue and disease labels describe the line's origin. A dependency measured in one line is not a target-level fact.

purpose.text: Use a clinical side-effect node to identify the warning term and test whether its accession is also a DiseaseNode key.

limitations.text: An accession absent here was not named by a warning report in this release. That is not a claim the drug has no other adverse effects.

The vocabulary covers warning-recorded side effects only, not trial-observed events, and is not a MedDRA coding; it is a different node type from ADVERSE_EVENT, which holds openFDA MedDRA labels. A named warning term is not evidence that the drug caused the event.

claims.text: A side-effect or toxicity term that a drug-warning report names, identified by the ontology accession the report carries. It is a term node, not a disease and not an observed event in a trial.
The term accession from clinical_report.sideEffects.diseaseId, used unmodified: EFO_, HP_, MONDO_, PATO_, NCIT_, OMIT_, ZP_, MP_ or MPATH_ prefixed. 199 accessions occur.

The node carries no label because six accessions occur under more than one source spelling; the report's own wording is on the HAS_SIDE_EFFECT edge. 118 of the 199 accessions are also DiseaseNode keys and join by string equality; 81 are absent from the release's disease set.
The release's harmonised development-stage code, computed from phaseFromSource, source and trialOverallStatus; one of 13 codes including UNKNOWN, APPROVAL, PHASE_4 and WITHDRAWAL.

The document class the build assigned from clinical_report.type: INDICATION for a report stating a drug-disease use, SAFETY for a warning record. The property is named reportType because `type` is the record kind in the graph's file format.
The source family the build assigned: CLINICAL_TRIAL, CURATED_RESOURCE, DRUG_LABEL or REGULATORY_AGENCY.
The reference the report was read from, for example ClinicalTrials.gov, TTD, DailyMed, ATC, EMA, FDA or PMDA.
The pipeline that supplied the record: AACT, ChEMBL, EMA, PMDA or TTD.
The sponsor name the registry recorded.
The sponsor's registry class: INDUSTRY, NIH, OTHER_GOV, NETWORK, FED, INDIV or OTHER.
The stage string exactly as the source stated it, before harmonisation (for example PHASE2, phase 1/phase 2, withdrawn, black box warning).
The registry's own phase code (PHASE1, PHASE1/PHASE2, PHASE2/PHASE3, PHASE4, EARLY_PHASE1); null on non-registry rows and where the registry recorded none.
The registry's recruitment and availability status (COMPLETED, TERMINATED, RECRUITING, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, UNKNOWN, ...); not a study result.
The sponsor's free-text reason for ending the study.
Classifier labels assigned to a stopped study, up to three per row; Uncategorised is the classifier's fallback, not a sponsor's reason.
The markets a drug warning was issued in, split from the warning's own semicolon string; filled on the 2,744 SAFETY rows only and as free text with no country code scheme.
The registry's brief summary of the study, as free text.
The registered title as the sponsor wrote it.
The report heading: the registered title when one exists, otherwise a sentence the build generated from the stage, first drug and first disease.
The registry's declared primary purpose (TREATMENT, PREVENTION, BASIC_SCIENCE, DIAGNOSTIC, ...); null is not the OTHER code.
The registry's design class, kept to three values: INTERVENTIONAL, OBSERVATIONAL or EXPANDED_ACCESS.
The number of arms the registry recorded; a null is not zero arms.
The date the study began; 1900-01-31 and 2099-01-01 are registry placeholders, not measured starts.
The year a drug warning was issued; filled on warning rows only and not the year of a trial or an approval.
The source record's address; not a key, because one source document can back several reports.
Flags naming a reason a consumer may drop the report (NO_DISEASE, UNVALIDATED_INDICATION, INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE, PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED, SAFETY_REPORT); flagged rows stay published.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's clinical report record.

limitations.text: A report absent here is outside the release's clinical sources. A null trial column means a non-registry row or an unrecorded fact, never a zero. A null diseases container is a list the build withdrew whole (qualityControls NO_DISEASE), not proof the document named none.
clinicalStage is not a development ladder. No column records a trial's outcome or target.
Each drug in a report is not necessarily studied for each disease in the same report; the report's drug and disease lists are not a pairing.
A COMPLETED report is not a successful one and a TERMINATED one is not a failed one; no field records whether the study worked.
Trial status does not measure efficacy or safety.
On registry rows the drug and disease names come from an extraction model, not from the registry's intervention and condition fields.
diseaseFromSource does not quote the condition the sponsor registered; on registry rows the drug and disease names come from an extraction model.

claims.text: origin separates registry trials (CLINICAL_TRIAL) from curated resources, drug labels and regulatory records; only registry rows carry trial columns. reportType is the document class (INDICATION or SAFETY) and is a different axis from origin. clinicalStage is the release's harmonised code, trialPhase the registry's own spelling. year dates a warning, trialStartDate a study.

One document a clinical source published: a registered trial, a drug label, an approval record, or a withdrawal or warning notice. The row is the source document, not a drug-disease pair, a study arm or a trial site.
clinical_report.id, the source's own identifier lower-cased: a registry number, a UUID, a 64-hex hash, a product number or a bare name. It is unique over all 289,954 rows.
The report's drugs and diseases are lists, not a pairing: one report naming two drugs and two diseases asserts no individual drug-disease pair.
58,965 of the 289,954 rows are labels, approvals and warnings rather than trials.
clinicalStage is a 13-code label and APPROVAL folds in registry statuses and reference lists.

purpose.text: Use this value to reach the paper's PubMed Central deposit.

limitations.text: Null when the paper has no PMC deposit, so no full text was mined.
Absence is not a missing publication record; the PMID remains the identity.

claims.text: PMC-prefixed text used as a cross-reference, not as the node key.
PubMed Central identifier of the publication where a PMC deposit exists.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's literature entry.

limitations.text: The node set is the release's text-mined corpus: a paper the release cites but its matcher grounds no entity in has no node. An evidence row with no PMID also has none; it is not a publication with an empty title.
A publication node records that the release cites the paper. It does not mean the paper's claims were verified by this graph.

claims.text: Most keys are PubMed ids; 899,451 of 21,938,364 are not. The key is the release's spelling, not a promise that a PubMed record exists.
A literature entry the release cites, identified by the release's literature key. The same entry is one node regardless of how many studies or evidence rows cite it.
The release literature key, normally a PubMed id but also PPR, PMC, IND, CAIN, ADL, FNI and other Europe PMC keys. A PMCID is a cross-reference and can be absent.

purpose.text: Use this value for external links.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not the join key and a weaker identity test than disease.id.

claims.text: Full ontology IRI of the disease term, copied from the source.
The base address varies within one prefix family.

purpose.text: Use this value as the term's display label.

limitations.text: Never null or empty in 26.09.
Not a join key; whitespace padding and re-labelling break exact matching.

claims.text: Preferred label of the ontology term.
Display text spanning diseases, phenotypes, measurements and non-Latin scripts.

purpose.text: Use this value as background context for the term.

limitations.text: Null when the ontology supplies no definition, not evidence that the concept is undefined.
Do not parse prose thresholds or treat it as a curated disease summary.

claims.text: Free-text definition asserted by the term's owning ontology.
Unstructured context whose voice and length vary by ontology.

purpose.text: Use this value to identify a therapeutic-area grouping root.

limitations.text: Never null; false is a definite non-membership.
Some flagged terms are not diseases, so the flag is not a clinical-content filter.

claims.text: Whether the term is one of the release's therapeutic-area grouping roots.
Boolean from the ontology subset tag; true marks a grouping root, not a graph root.

purpose.text: Use this value as the release's leaf flag.

limitations.text: Never null; false therefore carries no information.
Do not infer a leaf from this flag; test the children or descendants edge instead.

claims.text: Leaf flag on the disease ontology record.
Reads false on every 26.09 row because the build evaluated it before children were populated.

purpose.text: Use this value as the source URL of the ontology term.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It corroborates nothing beyond the source pointer and is not an independent identifier.

claims.text: Source URL of the ontology term, taken from disease.ontology.sources.url.
External address; it often equals code but may use a different base.

purpose.text: Use this value as the short source identifier of the term's ontology.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Do not render it as a name or join on it; use disease.id for identity.

claims.text: Short source identifier stored in disease.ontology.sources.name.
Despite the property name it is the term's accession, not its label.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's disease or phenotype term record, reading ontology.isTherapeuticArea and ontology.leaf to distinguish a therapeutic area, a leaf term and an internal ontology term.

limitations.text: A term absent here is not in the release's disease vocabulary; it is not evidence that the disease does not exist.
disease.id is not a MONDO-only identifier and the same biological concept can appear under more than one accession. Do not assume a single hierarchy or a single namespace.

claims.text: A disease or phenotype term used by the release. The node includes EFO, MONDO, Orphanet, HPO and other ontology accessions; it is one term, not a rolled-up therapeutic area.
disease.id, the ontology accession as written in the release.
The id space is mixed-prefix.

purpose.text: Use this value as the molecule's preferred display name.

limitations.text: Never null; the build coalesces to the id when no name exists.
Not unique, because unrelated ChEMBL records share names; never join on it.

claims.text: ChEMBL's preferred molecule name, falling back to the first ChEMBL synonym and then the molecule id.
Mostly upper-case ChEMBL house style.

purpose.text: Use this value as the molecule's modality.

limitations.text: Never null; 'Unknown' means ChEMBL stated no molecule type.
Modality only: it says nothing about approval, druggability or drug-admission route.

claims.text: ChEMBL molecule_type, the therapeutic modality or chemical class of the molecule.
Title-case categorical vocabulary; the literal 'Unknown' marks a ChEMBL silence.

purpose.text: Use this value as the molecule's maximum clinical stage across all indications.

limitations.text: Never null; UNKNOWN covers both no report and unmappable source stages.
Not indication-specific and not evidence of efficacy; the roll-up uses unfiltered clinical reports.

claims.text: Most advanced clinical stage the molecule reached in any clinical report, across all indications.
Ordinal SCREAMING_SNAKE stages; APPROVAL is most advanced and UNKNOWN last, with withdrawal and phase 4 collapsed to APPROVAL.

purpose.text: Use this value with inchiKey and molblock to look up the molecule's structure.

limitations.text: Null when ChEMBL holds no structure record, largely for biologics; it is not an empty structure.
Not a molecule identity key and not what the drug-page image renders.

claims.text: ChEMBL's canonical SMILES line notation for the molecule structure.
Structural lookup text.

purpose.text: Use this value as the molecule's structural lookup key.

limitations.text: Identifies a structure, not this row or a salt family.

claims.text: ChEMBL's InChIKey hash of the molecule structure.
Null exactly when canonicalSmiles is null, because the key derives from structure.
Fixed structural lookup value, not sortable and not decomposable into fields.

purpose.text: Use this value as the molecule's display summary.

limitations.text: Never null; clauses drop when data is missing.
Its indication counts do not reconcile with clinical_indication rows; never parse it as data.

claims.text: Build-generated sentence giving the molecule's modality, maximum clinical stage and approved and investigational indication counts.
A rendering rather than source text; its counts come from all clinical reports without a QC filter.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's ChEMBL molecule record.

limitations.text: A molecule absent here is outside the release's drug universe; it is not necessarily inactive or absent from ChEMBL.
A molecule is not a product or a salt: parent and child molecules are separate nodes and the parent relation is explicit.

claims.text: A bioactive molecule in the release's ChEMBL-derived drug set. It may be an approved drug, a clinical candidate or a tool compound.
drug_molecule.id, the ChEMBL molecule identifier.
drugType and maximumClinicalStage describe the molecule across all indications; neither is an indication-specific approval.

purpose.text: Use the code to select one constraint family before comparing values.

limitations.text: The release's constraint array never carries a null constraintType.
The three families are separate metrics; their scores are not comparable.

claims.text: The constraint metric family reported on this node.
The node key.
mis is missense, lof is loss of function, syn is synonymous.

purpose.text: Compare constraint values only within one family.

limitations.text: A gene with no constraint edge has no metric in the release, which is not a value of zero.
Constraint is a population-variation depletion signal, not a measured essentiality or a statement that loss of function is pathogenic.

claims.text: A constraint metric family: missense (mis), loss of function (lof) or synonymous (syn). The node names the family; each target's values are on the HAS_CONSTRAINT edge.
constraint_type::constraintType, one of mis, lof and syn.
The same gene has up to three constraint edges, one per family.

purpose.text: Use this value with position to locate the set's lead variant.

limitations.text: Never null; unusable chromosomes reject the row rather than nulling it.
Its value set differs from the variant and colocalisation chromosome columns; it is not the locus span.

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome of the set's lead variant, stored without a chr prefix.
Categorical string from 1-22, X and Y.

purpose.text: Use this value to locate the set's lead variant.

limitations.text: Never null.
The lead's position, not the fine-mapped interval and not a causal coordinate.

claims.text: One-based GRCh38 position of the set's lead variant.
Base pairs; always paired with chromosome.

purpose.text: Use this value to read the fine-mapped region as text; parse it tolerantly.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, whose method publishes no window here.
Null does not mean the set has no region; prefer the integer locus bounds where populated.

claims.text: Text start and end of the fine-mapped region, in one of two incompatible formats.
Either chr-prefixed or bare and zero-based text.

purpose.text: Use this value as the lead variant's effect size.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no estimate, not a measured zero.
Never pool across finemappingMethod; a SuSiE beta is a shrunk posterior mean.

claims.text: Effect size of the lead variant with respect to its alternate allele.
Sign gives ALT-allele direction; scale comes from the producing pipeline and is comparable only within a study.

purpose.text: Use this value as the lead variant's signed association statistic.

limitations.text: Null on every non-SuSiE-inf row, so a null is a method boundary rather than an absence of association.
It describes only the SuSiE-inf subset and cannot characterise the whole file's signal strength.

claims.text: Signed association statistic for the lead variant, beta divided by its standard error.
Standard-error units, sharing beta's polarity.

purpose.text: Use this value only with pValueExponent.

limitations.text: Never null at lead level in 26.09.
An unconditioned study p-value, not a posterior probability; sorting on it alone gives the wrong order.

claims.text: Mantissa half of the lead variant's study p-value, with p equal to mantissa times ten to the exponent.
Range 1.0 to 10.0.

purpose.text: Use this value with pValueMantissa.

limitations.text: Never null at lead level in 26.09.
Not the set's posterior evidence; a null here would mean the member-level field was read instead.

claims.text: Base-10 exponent half of the lead variant's study p-value.
Negative integer; smaller means stronger and it is read with the mantissa.

purpose.text: Use this value as the lead variant's effect-allele frequency.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no frequency, overwhelmingly molecular-QTL and curated-top-hit rows; not frequency zero.
Not a reference-panel frequency; filtering non-null restricts analysis to studies that reported it.

claims.text: Frequency of the lead variant's effect allele as the source study reported it.
Proportion from 0 to 1, specific to the study's ancestry and allele coding.

purpose.text: Use this value as the standard error of the lead variant's beta.

limitations.text: Null when the source published no standard error, not a precision of zero.
Some pipelines publish placeholder or member-level values, so it is not always the study's estimate.

claims.text: Standard error of the lead variant's beta.
Effect-size units; beta divided by it approximates the z-score, and zero is suspect.

purpose.text: Use this value to identify the fine-mapping method that produced the set.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A pipeline label, not a model specification or a quality rank.

claims.text: Fine-mapping algorithm that produced the set's posteriors.
Categorical values SuSie, SuSiE-inf and PICS; case-sensitive, and the method predicts which columns are populated.

purpose.text: Use this value to order the sets returned for a study region.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, whose method does not enumerate signals.
The first index is not the causal set, and a non-null filter is a method filter in disguise.

claims.text: One-based ordinal of this set among the sets returned for its study region, up to ten.
Ordinal position, not an importance ranking; most populated rows are index 1.

purpose.text: Use this value as the set's model evidence.

limitations.text: Null on every PICS row, which returns no model evidence; null is not weak evidence.
Orthogonal to resolution; read it with set size and never as a probability.

claims.text: Base-10 log Bayes factor that the credible set contains a causal variant.
Unbounded model evidence; higher is stronger and values span many orders of magnitude.

purpose.text: Use this value with set size to read the mean within-set linkage disequilibrium.

limitations.text: Null where the pipeline computed no within-set LD; not a purity of zero.
Read it with set size; high purity is not good resolution.

claims.text: Mean pairwise linkage-disequilibrium R-squared among the set's member variants.
Zero to one; near one means little internal resolution, while a low value means the set spans weakly linked variants.

purpose.text: Use this value with set size to read the minimum within-set linkage disequilibrium.

limitations.text: Null where no within-set LD was computed, not zero LD.
Method-specific floors are not global; do not threshold the whole column.

claims.text: Minimum pairwise linkage-disequilibrium R-squared within the credible set.
Zero to one; a single-member set reads 1 trivially.

purpose.text: Use this value as the study-level sample size attached to the set.

limitations.text: Null where the study index surfaced no usable total, not a small study.
Not for power calculations and not always a real cohort size.

claims.text: Study-level sample size copied onto the credible set.
Rough study attribute; many rows share a few values.

purpose.text: Use this value to read the fine-mapping provenance of the set.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09; the documented unknown class does not occur.
Not association strength or effect size; never sort the labels alphabetically.

claims.text: Fine-mapping framework and linkage-disequilibrium source behind the set, as a four-value label.
Ordinal provenance, best first; 26.09 stores long labels such as 'SuSiE fine-mapped credible set with in-sample LD'.

purpose.text: Use this value with isTransQtl to read the study design.

limitations.text: Never null; unknown designs are excluded upstream.
Says nothing about tissue or condition; read the joined study for those.

claims.text: Study design behind the credible set: gwas or one of five molecular QTL classes.
Lower-case categorical code copied from the study.

purpose.text: Use this value with studyType to read whether the molecular-QTL signal is trans.

limitations.text: Populated on all molecular-QTL classes despite the name, and the deciding distance is not published.

claims.text: Whether the molecular-QTL lead variant lies more than five megabases from the gene whose molecular trait is measured.
Boolean cis/trans flag from a fixed five-megabase window.
Null on exactly the GWAS rows, where cis and trans are undefined; false is measured cis.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's fine-mapped credible set record.

limitations.text: No credible set means the study has no fine-mapped locus in the release, not that no association exists.
A credible set is a statistical set, not a biological mechanism. Membership does not establish causality; the L2G edge is a prediction.

claims.text: A 95% credible set from a GWAS or molecular QTL study, with the lead variant, fine-mapping method and summary statistics.
credible_set.studyLocusId. It is unique in the release and names one study-locus credible set, not one variant.
credibleSetIndex orders sets within a study locus. The lead variant is the variant with the highest posterior probability, not the causal variant.

purpose.text: Use this value with position to locate the variant; cast before numeric sorting.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
A chr-prefixed or numeric filter matches nothing; it is not the gene's chromosome property.

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome label of the variant, stored without a chr prefix.
Categorical string from 1-22, X, Y and MT.

purpose.text: Use this value to locate the variant.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Indels are left-anchored representations, not unique biological points; never join on position alone.

claims.text: One-based leftmost GRCh38 coordinate of the variant representation.
Base pairs; meaningful only with chromosome and both alleles.

purpose.text: Use this value with chromosome, position and alternateAllele to identify the variant.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It reproduces variantId only with chromosome, position and alternateAllele; it is not a transcript effect.

claims.text: Reference allele string on the GRCh38 forward strand.
Nucleotide letters or indel gap representation; multi-base values occur.

purpose.text: Use this value as the effect allele for frequencies and effect directions.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Only SNVs and small indels are represented; it is not a genotype or haplotype.

claims.text: Alternate, or effect, allele string on the GRCh38 forward strand.
The allele against which allele frequencies and effect directions are measured.

purpose.text: Use this value as the variant's genomic HGVS label.

limitations.text: Null on a few rows where no genomic description was produced.
Not unique and not a key; coding and protein HGVS forms are different strings.

claims.text: Genomic HGVS description taken from the first transcript consequence, or the first intergenic consequence.
Genomic-level label independent of any chosen transcript.

purpose.text: Use this value as the variant's display summary.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
It names whichever transcript sorted first, adds no information beyond its source columns and is unstable across builds.

claims.text: Build-generated sentence summarising the variant's most severe consequence and nearest gene context.
Display text assembled from consequence, transcript and distance fields.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's variant record.

limitations.text: A variant absent here has no phenotypic information in the release; it is not absent from the human genome.
The id is build-dependent and allele-spelled; a liftover or a different representation is a different string. Do not join on rsID without an explicit cross-reference.

claims.text: A variant in the release's variant universe. The identity is the release's variant id, not an rsID or a normalized VCF record.
variant.variantId, spelled chromosome_position_reference_alternate (for example 1_17005_A_G). rsIds are cross-references, not the key.
MostSevereConsequence is a separate edge to an SO term. A variant's effects are target- and transcript-specific records, not properties of the variant alone.

purpose.text: Use approvedSymbol as the display label.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09; an ENSG-shaped value marks a missing HGNC symbol.
Not unique; shared symbols occur, so never join on it. Use target.id.

claims.text: HGNC's current approved gene symbol, with the Ensembl gene id as the fallback.
Display label; HGNC renames propagate between releases.

purpose.text: Search and display text; trim before exact comparison.

limitations.text: Never null but empty when neither HGNC nor Ensembl supplies a name.
Not unique; many pseudogenes share a description, so do not use it as identity.

claims.text: HGNC's approved full gene name, falling back to the Ensembl description and then the empty string.

purpose.text: Use biotype to separate protein-coding genes from non-coding and pseudogene targets.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09; the empty string is the renamed tecRNA class, not an unknown biotype.
Non-protein-coding does not mean non-target; transcript biotype is a separate unstripped vocabulary.

claims.text: Ensembl gene biotype after the build removes the substring 'tec' from the stored string.
Categorical Ensembl vocabulary; 'protein_coding' is the usual drug-target subset.

purpose.text: Use functionDescriptions as context only.

limitations.text: Null when no UniProt entry is mapped, or empty when the entry has no function block.
Not a controlled annotation and not evidence of a role in any disease.

claims.text: UniProt free-text descriptions of the gene product's function, one element per function block.
Context only; the text retains UniProt citation markers and line-join artefacts.

purpose.text: Filter and group targets by chromosome.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target; unmapped scaffolds are absent rather than labelled.
A variant inside this span is not necessarily in a transcript.

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome of the gene's genomic span, stored without a chr prefix.
Categorical string from 1-22, X, Y and MT; lexical sorting is wrong.

purpose.text: Read start with end to place the gene's genomic span.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
The gene span includes introns and UTRs; it is not a transcript or coding start.

claims.text: Lowest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the gene's genomic span.
Base pairs; always less than or equal to end within one row.

purpose.text: Read end together with chromosome and start.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
Not the end of a translated product; the span includes introns and UTRs.

claims.text: Highest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the gene's genomic span.
Base pairs.

purpose.text: Use strand to read the direction of transcription.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
Not a transcript-level strand and not interchangeable with the '+'/'-' spelling used elsewhere.

claims.text: Direction of transcription as the signed integer 1 (forward) or -1 (reverse).
No zero or unknown state; it selects start or end as the transcription start site.

purpose.text: Read tss as the canonical transcription start site.

limitations.text: Never null for a keyed target.
Canonical is GENCODE's display choice, not MANE Select; the coordinate is not a promoter boundary.

claims.text: Transcription start site of the gene's canonical transcript on GRCh38.
One-based coordinate; equals start on the forward strand and end on the reverse strand.

purpose.text: Use approvedSymbol for display and id for joins.

limitations.text: A gene absent from this node set is not a target in the release; it may still exist in Ensembl. A null symbol is a release gap, not a non-gene.
Target membership is the release's target universe, not all human genes. Protein-level claims need the protein identifiers, not this node.

claims.text: A human gene/protein product with an Ensembl gene identifier. The target is the gene the release's evidence and drug records refer to; it is not a specific protein isoform or transcript.
target.id, the Ensembl gene accession (ENSG...). A target row is one gene; the identifier is stable while symbols and coordinates move.
biotype separates protein-coding genes from non-coding and pseudogene targets.

purpose.text: Use name as the cell line's display label; the SIDM id is the key.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no name.
Do not use the label as identity; names are not unique.

claims.text: The cell-line name supplied by the CRISPR screen.
A source label for display; the SIDM id is the key.

purpose.text: Read tissue as the screen's tissue label for display or grouping.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no tissue label.
Tissue labels are not normalised and do not replace a biosample id.

claims.text: The tissue label supplied by the CRISPR screen.
A source label, not a biosample ontology key.

purpose.text: Use tissue_id to report the tissue identifier the screen supplied.

limitations.text: Null when the screen supplies no tissue id.
No crosswalk to BiosampleNode is supplied by the release.

claims.text: The tissue identifier supplied by the CRISPR screen.
An ontology-style id where supplied; it is not a biosample id.

purpose.text: Use a CRISPR cell-line node to identify the cell line behind a CRISPR screen.

limitations.text: A screen without a cell-line id emits no TESTED_IN edge.
A SIDM line is not a DepMap line; do not join the two id spaces. The screen result is an in-vitro observation.

claims.text: A cell line used by a CRISPR screen, identified by the release's SIDM cell-line id in evidence_crispr.diseaseCellLines.
diseaseCellLines.id (SIDM). The release supplies no crosswalk to the DepMap ACH ids used by target_essentiality, so these are a separate node space from CELL_LINE.
The name/tissue fields are source labels, not ontology keys.

purpose.text: Use source with identifier to place the cross-reference in its namespace.

limitations.text: An absent value means the release listed no authority for the identifier.
Casing and vocabulary differ by dataset, so the source alone does not prove the external record exists.

claims.text: Authority or namespace that issued the cross-reference identifier.
Names the authority, such as Ensembl, UniProt, Reactome, DrugBank or ClinVar, not the entity type.

purpose.text: Use identifier with source to name an external record.

limitations.text: An absent identifier means the release listed no accession for that authority.
Not necessarily a resolvable or unique accession, and two entities sharing it are not thereby identical.

claims.text: Accession or identifier string within the namespace named by source.
Meaningful only together with source; identifier formats are namespace-specific.

purpose.text: Use a cross-reference node to join a release entity to an external namespace.

limitations.text: An absent cross-reference means the release did not list it.
Two entities sharing a cross-reference are not thereby the same entity; the edge means 'has this identifier', not identity.

claims.text: An external identifier, stored once per (source, identifier) pair. It is the join surface between the release's entities and external namespaces.
(source, identifier), written source:identifier in edges.
The source names the authority (Ensembl, UniProt, Reactome, DrugBank, ClinVar, ...), not the entity type.

purpose.text: Use term as the retired accession for historical matching.

limitations.text: The release's obsoleteTerms arrays never carry a null element.
The string is retained for historical matching only; the namespace prefix does not prove a current record exists.

claims.text: The retired ontology accession as the release spells it.
The node key, prefixed obsolete_term::.
Values use the release's underscore separator, for example GO_0033490 or CHEBI_22318, and are not CURIEs.

purpose.text: Use an obsolete-term node to keep a retired ontology accession addressable for historical matching.

limitations.text: No node means the release lists no such retired accession. The release names no successor, merging or split for a retired accession.
A retired accession is not a synonym of its replacement and cannot be resolved to a current term from this dataset, so the edge does not link to the DISEASE node of the same string.

claims.text: A retired ontology accession that a disease or phenotype term lists as an obsolete term. It is an accession, not a term record of the dataset that lists it.
The accession as written, keyed obsolete_term::accession. The same accession listed by several current terms is one node.

None of the 9,852 obsoleteTerms elements in disease resolves to a disease.id or a disease_hpo.id, and none of the 5,955 in disease_hpo resolves to a disease_hpo.id; the 297 disease_hpo obsoleteTerms values that also occur in the disease table stay retired accessions. The node set keeps the retired accession addressable instead of dangling or being dropped.

purpose.text: Use this value as the term's name.

limitations.text: Never null or empty in both source datasets.
The same label need not denote the same term across HP and MP; join on the accession.

claims.text: HPO or MP label; casing follows the source vocabulary.
Preferred label of the phenotype term in its source ontology.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's phenotype term.

limitations.text: A term absent here is outside the release's phenotype subset.
A phenotype annotation is an association, not a diagnosis. A mouse phenotype mapped to a human term is a model inference.

claims.text: The label is the term's preferred name; the accession is the key. A disease-phenotype relation and a mouse-phenotype relation are different edges.

A phenotype or ontology term used by the release's disease-phenotype and mouse-phenotype records. The vocabulary is mixed: disease_hpo contains HP, UBERON, GO, CHEBI, CL, PATO, PR, MPATH and other accessions, and mouse records use MP terms.
The ontology accession, prefixed phenotype:: in keys. Different vocabularies must not be merged even when accessions collide.

purpose.text: Use label to compare a disease synonym string exactly.

limitations.text: The release's four synonym arrays never carry a null element.
Two disease terms can share a label, and the same label can appear under two classes; the node is a vocabulary entry, not a disease.

claims.text: The synonym string as the release spells it.
Part of the node key, with kind.
Case, punctuation and whitespace are as supplied; there is no normalization.

purpose.text: Use kind to select the synonym class the string was recorded under.

limitations.text: The four classes are release fields, not an ontology of synonym scopes; their definitions are not restated in the dataset.

claims.text: The synonym class the string was recorded under.
Part of the node key, with label.
Every synonym node names exactly one class.
exact comes from exactSynonyms, related from relatedSynonyms, narrow from narrowSynonyms and broad from broadSynonyms.

purpose.text: Use a disease-synonym node to match a disease name under its recorded synonym class.

limitations.text: No node means the release lists no such name for any disease term. The synonym arrays carry no source, curator or date, so a name node cannot say who asserted the name.

A synonym is a naming fact, not an equivalence claim: an exact synonym does not merge two DISEASE nodes, a broad synonym is wider than the term and a narrow synonym is narrower. The release supplies no synonym source field, so source is unresolved for this domain.

claims.text: A name the release lists for a disease term, qualified by the synonym class it was recorded under.
(kind, label), keyed disease_synonym::kind::label. The same string under two classes is two nodes, because the release records the classes separately.

kind is the release's synonym class: exact, related, narrow or broad. disease.synonyms repeats the four flat arrays field for field (93,524 exact, 14,670 related, 1,909 narrow and 1,523 broad elements, with no row differing), so the struct supplies no additional nodes.

purpose.text: Use it to select warnings by toxicity category.

limitations.text: A null is a release gap, not 'no toxicity'.
The category is a label given by the source, not a severity grade.

claims.text: The release's toxicity category for the warning, for example hepatotoxicity or cardiotoxicity.
Null for 246 rows.

purpose.text: Read the string as a list when it contains semicolons; it is not an ISO code.

limitations.text: A jurisdiction is not a marketing authorisation for the molecule.

claims.text: The regulatory jurisdiction or jurisdictions named by the warning, sometimes a semicolon-separated list.

purpose.text: Use it to read the warning's published text.

limitations.text: The text is quoted source prose, not a normalised statement of effect.

claims.text: Free-text description of the warning as published.
Null for 1,024 rows; the warning still exists as a node.

purpose.text: Use it to tell a black box warning from a withdrawal.

limitations.text: A withdrawal is not the same statement as a boxed warning, and neither is an adverse event report.
The two classes are different regulatory actions; do not pool them as 'safety'.

claims.text: The warning class used by the release: 'Black Box Warning' or 'Withdrawn' in 26.09.

purpose.text: Use it to date a warning.

limitations.text: A null year is a release gap, not an undated event.
The year is the source's warning year, not the first approval or the first report.

claims.text: The year recorded for the warning.
Null for 1,028 rows.

purpose.text: Use it to read the disease context of a warning.

limitations.text: A null means the warning carries no disease context in this release.
The label is source vocabulary, not a DiseaseNode name unless efoId resolves in the release.

claims.text: The disease or phenotype label the release associates with the warning.
Null for 1,057 rows.

purpose.text: Use it to resolve a warning's disease context to an accession.

limitations.text: A null id does not mean the warning lacks a disease context.
The accession is not guaranteed to be a DiseaseNode in 26.09; resolve it before joining.

claims.text: The EFO accession paired with efoTerm where the release supplies one.
It is the warning's disease context; the release does not materialise a warning-to-disease edge from it in this layer.
Null for 1,057 rows.

purpose.text: Use it to resolve a warning's toxicity class to an accession.

limitations.text: The class accession is not the same fact as efoId, which describes the warning's disease context.

claims.text: The EFO accession the release uses for the warning's toxicity class.
Null for 246 rows, which are the rows with no toxicityClass.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's regulatory warning record; the molecules it names are attached by the HAS_DRUG_WARNING edge.

limitations.text: A warning absent here is not in the release's warning set. A null country, year, toxicity class or description is a gap in the source row, not a property of the warning.

A warning is regulatory label text, not an observed adverse event, an incidence rate or a causal finding. Warnings are not deduplicated across countries or years, so the same concern can appear in several nodes.

claims.text: A drug warning row from ChEMBL: a labelled safety concern of a molecule, with its regulatory jurisdiction, warning type, year and disease context where the release supplies one.
drug_warning.id cast to text and prefixed drug_warning::. The release's id is unique across its 2,009 warning rows.

warningType separates a black box warning from a withdrawal. efoTerm/efoId name the warning's disease context where present; a null EFO field is a release gap, not an assertion that the warning has no disease context.

purpose.text: Read it together with source; the string alone has no namespace.

limitations.text: The same string can denote different records under different sources.

claims.text: The identifier assigned by the citing source, for example a PMID or DOI.

purpose.text: Use source with referenceId to place the reference in its namespace.

limitations.text: Do not read source as the warning's country; it qualifies referenceId.

claims.text: The namespace or publisher of the reference, for example PubMed, WHO or DOI.
The source qualifies referenceId.

purpose.text: Use url to open or cite the referenced document.

limitations.text: A locator is not a guarantee that the resource is reachable or supports the warning.

claims.text: The URL recorded for the reference.

purpose.text: Use a warning reference node to resolve the document cited by a drug warning: read warning -> reference.

limitations.text: A warning whose references array is empty has no reference node or edge.
A citation is not evidence that the document supports every statement in the warning, and different sources can reuse the same identifier string.

claims.text: A document or record cited by a drug warning, identified by its source namespace and the source's own identifier.
The (source, id) pair, keyed source::id. A pair always carries the same url in 26.09.
id is the source's identifier (PMID, DOI, document number); source is its namespace or publisher.

purpose.text: Use id as the evidence record's node key.

limitations.text: Do not carry the id across releases: a changed input mints a new hash. The hash covers the row's identity fields, not its free text or score, unless the source's own definition says otherwise.

claims.text: The source row's id.
The value is a build-assigned SHA-1 content hash in all twenty sources, not a ClinVar, ClinGen, COSMIC or UniProt accession. It is unique within the released table, so it is the node key.

purpose.text: Use datasourceId to tell which source supplied the evidence.

limitations.text: The code is a reporting label; it does not encode the evidence method.

claims.text: The release's datasource code for the evidence row.
The value is constant within each source table and names the source, not the assay.

purpose.text: Use datatypeId to group evidence by the release's broad evidence type.

limitations.text: Two sources sharing a datatypeId are not measuring the same thing.

claims.text: The release's evidence-type bucket for the row.

The value is constant within a source table and groups sources into broad buckets such as genetic_association, affected_pathway or literature. It is not a measurement type or a controlled assay vocabulary.

purpose.text: Use score to compare evidence only within one source.

limitations.text: Do not compare scores across sources or with an aggregate association score. A constant score, such as 1.0 for reactome and cancer_biomarkers, ranks nothing.

claims.text: The release's per-row evidence score.
The score is already on the source's own scale. Its range and meaning differ by source and it is not a probability or a p-value.

purpose.text: Use resourceScore to read the source's native quantity for the row.

limitations.text: The native quantity and its scale differ by source. A null resourceScore means the source has no such column, not that the row scored zero.

claims.text: The source's native score where the dataset publishes one.

resourceScore is the source's own quantity (for example a raw literature mention count or a fine-mapping score), not a rescaled version of score. It is null on the eleven sources that do not publish one.

purpose.text: Use publicationDate to date the evidence by the earliest publication the source attaches to the row.

limitations.text: A null date is a source or citation gap; it is not an undated claim. The field is a string, not a normalised date, and some values lie outside the plausible publication range.

claims.text: The earliest publication date the source attaches to the row.
The value is a source-supplied date string. clingen has no publicationDate column at all and carries releaseDate instead.

purpose.text: Use evidenceDate to place the evidence row in time as the release records it.

limitations.text: Do not use it as a trustworthy real-world event date without checking the source. A null is a release gap, not a zero.

claims.text: The release's evidence date for the row.
The value is a source-supplied date string. Many sources copy publicationDate into it; clinical_precedence uses it for a separate date and contains values up to 2099.

purpose.text: Use qualityControls to see the flags the release attached to the record.

limitations.text: The flags are source-specific and not a common QC vocabulary. An empty array does not mean the source validated the row cleanly.

claims.text: The release's quality-control flags for the row.
The array holds the flags the release attached to this evidence record. An empty array is common and is not a claim that the row passed every check.

purpose.text: Use targetFromSourceId to trace the resolved target back to the name the source wrote.

limitations.text: Do not join it to target.id. One symbol can resolve to more than one target, and an alias can resolve to a different gene.

claims.text: The target as the source wrote it, before resolution.
This is the source's gene symbol or accession, not necessarily an Ensembl id. The resolved target is the HAS_TARGET edge.

purpose.text: Use diseaseFromSourceMappedId to trace the resolved disease back to the accession the release mapped.

limitations.text: Do not anti-join this column against disease.id and read the misses as broken references; some sources deliberately carry retired accessions.

claims.text: The source's disease accession before the release mapped it to diseaseId.
The mapped accession can be a retired or non-current term. The resolved disease is the HAS_DISEASE edge, not this property.

purpose.text: Use diseaseFromSource to read the disease label the source wrote.

limitations.text: Two spellings can denote one disease and one label can cover several terms.

claims.text: The disease label as the source wrote it.
The value is free text, not an ontology id. The resolved disease is the HAS_DISEASE edge.

purpose.text: Use diseaseFromSourceId to read the disease accession the source wrote.

limitations.text: Do not treat a source accession as a disease key without checking the mapping.

claims.text: The source's disease accession as written.
The accession is not guaranteed to be a current disease.id; the resolved term is the HAS_DISEASE edge.

purpose.text: Use studyId to read the study, panel or curation handle the source states.

limitations.text: Do not join studyId to study.studyId: every non-null value in these eight sources misses. The field does not identify a GWAS or QTL study row.

claims.text: The source's study, panel or curation handle.
No 26.09 evidence dataset carries a studyId that resolves to study.studyId. The values are COSMIC/ClinVar/PanelApp/G2P handles or array-accession strings, so they stay properties.

purpose.text: Use confidence to read the confidence or classification level the source assigns.

limitations.text: Do not compare confidence values across sources or treat a missing value as low confidence.

claims.text: The source's own confidence or classification level.
The scale belongs to the source: ClinGen classifications, ClinVar review status, Expression Atlas low/medium/high, or UniProt high/medium. The strings are not a release-wide confidence scale.

purpose.text: Use directionOnTrait to read the source's stated direction of effect on the trait.

limitations.text: Do not infer direction from the target-disease score or from another source.

claims.text: The source's stated direction of effect on the trait.
Values are source-specific (for example risk or protect). A null means the source did not state a direction, not that the effect is neutral.

purpose.text: Use directionOnTarget to read the source's stated direction of effect.

limitations.text: A direction is the source's assertion, not a measured mechanism.

claims.text: The source's predicted direction of effect on the target.
The values are LoF and GoF where stated. A null means no direction was supplied; it is not a wild-type or neutral call.

purpose.text: Use targetFromSource to read the target label the source wrote.

limitations.text: Do not use it as a gene key.

claims.text: The target label as the source wrote it.
The value is free text; the resolved target is the HAS_TARGET edge.

purpose.text: Use targetModulation to read the source's statement of how the target is modulated.

limitations.text: Do not map it to a direction or an action type without a curated mapping.

claims.text: The source's free-text statement of how the target is modulated.
The value is a source phrase, not a mechanism ontology term.

purpose.text: Use variantRsId to read the source's dbSNP cross-reference for the variant.

limitations.text: The rsID is often absent and many reported rsIDs have no variant row. Do not join on it without an explicit cross-reference.

claims.text: The variant's rsID as reported by the source.
The value is an external dbSNP cross-reference. The variant node key is the release's variantId and the HAS_VARIANT edge uses that, not the rsID.

purpose.text: Use variantFunctionalConsequenceId to group evidence by the consequence class the source names.

limitations.text: The spelling can differ from so.id (underscore versus colon) and is not normalised here. It is a property, not an SO edge.

claims.text: The source's Sequence Ontology consequence id.
The value names a consequence class; it is not an observed functional assay.

purpose.text: Use allelicRequirements to read the allelic requirement the source states for the association.

limitations.text: Do not infer a mode of inheritance from it without a curated mapping.

claims.text: The source's free-text allelic requirement for the association.
The array holds source phrases such as inheritance modes; it is not a controlled vocabulary.

purpose.text: Use clinicalSignificances to read the variant classifications the source reports.

limitations.text: Conflicting classifications can appear together. A pathogenic label on a variant does not establish that the target causes the disease.

claims.text: The ClinVar clinical-significance strings reported for the variant.
The array contains classifications such as pathogenic, benign or uncertain significance. It is not a direction of effect on the target.

purpose.text: Use alleleOrigins to read the germline or somatic origin the source states.

limitations.text: The array is free text and is not a controlled provenance vocabulary.

claims.text: The source's allele-origin strings.
The values describe germline or somatic origin where the source states it.

purpose.text: Use cohortPhenotypes to read the phenotype labels the source attaches to the cohort.

limitations.text: Do not treat a cohort label as a disease.id or as a phenotype node.

claims.text: The source's cohort phenotype labels.
The array holds free-text phenotype labels, not disease accessions.

purpose.text: clingen has no publicationDate and carries this instead; eva and eva_somatic carry both.

limitations.text: The value is a source date string, not a normalised release timestamp.

claims.text: The source release date for the record.

purpose.text: Use drugId to reach the molecule the source names for the drug context.

limitations.text: null means unmatched, not drug-free.

claims.text: The ChEMBL molecule id the source states for the drug context.
The value is a ChEMBL molecule id and resolves to drug_molecule.id on every non-null row in both sources. The HAS_MOLECULE edge carries it.
cancer_biomarkers leaves it null on 573 of 1,301 rows when no released molecule matched the reported name.

purpose.text: Use drugFromSource to read the drug name or family the source wrote.

limitations.text: Do not treat every value as a molecule name; only drugId resolves to a molecule.

claims.text: The drug name or family as the source wrote it.
The value is free text and can name a drug class rather than one molecule. cancer_biomarkers splits combination regimens into separate rows.

purpose.text: Use projectId to group evidence by the source's project.

limitations.text: It is a source handle, not a study key.

claims.text: The source project or screen identifier.
The value groups rows by the source's project, not by a study row.

purpose.text: Use cohortId to identify the source's cohort.

limitations.text: Cohorts are source-specific and do not share a vocabulary across datasets.

claims.text: The source cohort identifier.
The value identifies the source's cohort; it is not a clinical trial or a study.

purpose.text: Use contrast to read the conditions the row compares.

limitations.text: Contrast strings are source-specific and not a controlled vocabulary.

claims.text: The experimental contrast the row measures.
The value names the compared conditions, not a disease or a target.

purpose.text: Use variantFromSourceId to trace the row back to the source's variant record.

limitations.text: Do not use it as a variant node key.

claims.text: The source's variant record accession.
The value is a ClinVar/ClinVar-like record id (for example VCV...), not the release's variantId and not an rsID.

purpose.text: Use variantHgvsId to read the source's HGVS spelling of the variant.

limitations.text: HGVS strings are representation-dependent and are not joined to variant.variantId.

claims.text: The source's HGVS expression for the variant.
The value is a genomic HGVS string, not a variant node key.

purpose.text: Use a source evidence node as the released observation from one evidence source.

limitations.text: A missing source row is absent evidence, not a tested negative. A null provenance field means the source did not supply it.
An evidence node is not the aggregate association between its target and disease; the aggregate layer is separate and is not linked back to individual rows by the release.

claims.text: One row of a target-disease evidence dataset, kept as a node so its target, disease and provenance can be traversed. The node is the source's assertion, not an aggregate target-disease score.
The dataset's own id field. Every evidence id in 26.09 is a build-assigned hash, unique within the released table but not a provider accession and not stable across releases.

Every source node has one HAS_TARGET and one HAS_DISEASE edge. Source-specific provenance edges are HAS_VARIANT, FROM_STUDY, SUPPORTED_BY, TESTED_IN, FROM_MODEL, HAS_MODEL_PHENOTYPE, HAS_HUMAN_PHENOTYPE, HAS_MOLECULE and IN_PATHWAY.

purpose.text: Use id as the evidence record's node key.

limitations.text: Do not carry the id across releases: a changed input mints a new hash. The hash covers the row's identity fields, not its free text or score, unless the source's own definition says otherwise.

claims.text: The source row's id.
The value is a build-assigned SHA-1 content hash in all twenty sources, not a ClinVar, ClinGen, COSMIC or UniProt accession. It is unique within the released table, so it is the node key.

purpose.text: Use datasourceId to tell which source supplied the evidence.

limitations.text: The code is a reporting label; it does not encode the evidence method.

claims.text: The release's datasource code for the evidence row.
The value is constant within each source table and names the source, not the assay.

purpose.text: Use datatypeId to group evidence by the release's broad evidence type.

purpose.text: Use this node as the released Project Score CRISPR screen result for a target-disease association.

limitations.text: A row with no cell line would yield no TESTED_IN edge; this release has none.
The cell-line tissue fields live on the cell-line node, not this row. The TESTED_IN edge does not assert that the screen was successful.

claims.text: One Project Score whole-genome CRISPR screen result associating a target with a disease, with the assayed cell lines.
evidence_crispr.id; 517 rows and 517 distinct ids, none null. SHA-1 over targetId, targetFromSourceId, diseaseId and datasourceId; the score and cell lines sit outside the hash.

Every row names at least one cell line; diseaseCellLines expands to TESTED_IN edges keyed by the SIDM cell-line id. The release's CellLineNode is keyed by the DepMap depmapId (ACH), and no SIDM-to-ACH crosswalk is in 26.09, so these edges have no cell-line node. score and resourceScore are different scales (score 0.415-0.838, resourceScore 36-83.8).
publicationDate and evidenceDate are both 2024-01-11 on every row.

purpose.text: Use id as the evidence record's node key.

limitations.text: Do not carry the id across releases: a changed input mints a new hash. The hash covers the row's identity fields, not its free text or score, unless the source's own definition says otherwise.

claims.text: The source row's id.
The value is a build-assigned SHA-1 content hash in all twenty sources, not a ClinVar, ClinGen, COSMIC or UniProt accession. It is unique within the released table, so it is the node key.

purpose.text: Use datasourceId to tell which source supplied the evidence.

limitations.text: The code is a reporting label; it does not encode the evidence method.

claims.text: The release's datasource code for the evidence row.
The value is constant within each source table and names the source, not the assay.

purpose.text: Use datatypeId to group evidence by the release's broad evidence type.

limitations.text: Two sources sharing a datatypeId are not measuring the same thing.

claims.text: The release's evidence-type bucket for the row.

The value is constant within a source table and groups sources into broad buckets such as genetic_association, affected_pathway or literature. It is not a measurement type or a controlled assay vocabulary.

purpose.text: Use score to compare evidence only within one source.

limitations.text: Do not compare scores across sources or with an aggregate association score. A constant score, such as 1.0 for reactome and cancer_biomarkers, ranks nothing.

claims.text: The release's per-row evidence score.
The score is already on the source's own scale. Its range and meaning differ by source and it is not a probability or a p-value.

purpose.text: Use resourceScore to read the source's native quantity for the row.

limitations.text: The native quantity and its scale differ by source. A null resourceScore means the source has no such column, not that the row scored zero.

claims.text: The source's native score where the dataset publishes one.

resourceScore is the source's own quantity (for example a raw literature mention count or a fine-mapping score), not a rescaled version of score. It is null on the eleven sources that do not publish one.

purpose.text: Use publicationDate to date the evidence by the earliest publication the source attaches to the row.

limitations.text: A null date is a source or citation gap; it is not an undated claim. The field is a string, not a normalised date, and some values lie outside the plausible publication range.

claims.text: The earliest publication date the source attaches to the row.
The value is a source-supplied date string. clingen has no publicationDate column at all and carries releaseDate instead.

purpose.text: Use evidenceDate to place the evidence row in time as the release records it.

limitations.text: Do not use it as a trustworthy real-world event date without checking the source. A null is a release gap, not a zero.

claims.text: The release's evidence date for the row.
The value is a source-supplied date string. Many sources copy publicationDate into it; clinical_precedence uses it for a separate date and contains values up to 2099.

purpose.text: Use qualityControls to see the flags the release attached to the record.

limitations.text: The flags are source-specific and not a common QC vocabulary. An empty array does not mean the source validated the row cleanly.

claims.text: The release's quality-control flags for the row.

claims.text: The release's quality-control flags for the row.
The array holds the flags the release attached to this evidence record. An empty array is common and is not a claim that the row passed every check.

purpose.text: Use targetFromSourceId to trace the resolved target back to the name the source wrote.

limitations.text: Do not join it to target.id. One symbol can resolve to more than one target, and an alias can resolve to a different gene.

claims.text: The target as the source wrote it, before resolution.
This is the source's gene symbol or accession, not necessarily an Ensembl id. The resolved target is the HAS_TARGET edge.

purpose.text: Use diseaseFromSourceMappedId to trace the resolved disease back to the accession the release mapped.

limitations.text: Do not anti-join this column against disease.id and read the misses as broken references; some sources deliberately carry retired accessions.

claims.text: The source's disease accession before the release mapped it to diseaseId.
The mapped accession can be a retired or non-current term. The resolved disease is the HAS_DISEASE edge, not this property.

purpose.text: Use diseaseFromSource to read the disease label the source wrote.

limitations.text: Two spellings can denote one disease and one label can cover several terms.

claims.text: The disease label as the source wrote it.
The value is free text, not an ontology id. The resolved disease is the HAS_DISEASE edge.

purpose.text: Use diseaseFromSourceId to read the disease accession the source wrote.

limitations.text: Do not treat a source accession as a disease key without checking the mapping.

claims.text: The source's disease accession as written.
The accession is not guaranteed to be a current disease.id; the resolved term is the HAS_DISEASE edge.

purpose.text: Use studyId to read the study, panel or curation handle the source states.

limitations.text: Do not join studyId to study.studyId: every non-null value in these eight sources misses. The field does not identify a GWAS or QTL study row.

claims.text: The source's study, panel or curation handle.
No 26.09 evidence dataset carries a studyId that resolves to study.studyId. The values are COSMIC/ClinVar/PanelApp/G2P handles or array-accession strings, so they stay properties.

purpose.text: Use confidence to read the confidence or classification level the source assigns.

limitations.text: Do not compare confidence values across sources or treat a missing value as low confidence.

claims.text: The source's own confidence or classification level.

purpose.text: Use directionOnTrait to read the source's stated direction of effect on the trait.

limitations.text: Do not infer direction from the target-disease score or from another source.

claims.text: The source's stated direction of effect on the trait.
Values are source-specific (for example risk or protect). A null means the source did not state a direction, not that the effect is neutral.

purpose.text: Use directionOnTarget to read the source's stated direction of effect.

limitations.text: A direction is the source's assertion, not a measured mechanism.

claims.text: The source's predicted direction of effect on the target.
The values are LoF and GoF where stated. A null means no direction was supplied; it is not a wild-type or neutral call.

limitations.text: Do not use it as a gene key.

limitations.text: The spelling can differ from so.id (underscore versus colon) and is not normalised here. It is a property, not an SO edge.

claims.text: The source's Sequence Ontology consequence id.

purpose.text: Use allelicRequirements to read the allelic requirement the source states for the association.

limitations.text: Do not infer a mode of inheritance from it without a curated mapping.

claims.text: The source's free-text allelic requirement for the association.

purpose.text: Use alleleOrigins to read the germline or somatic origin the source states.

limitations.text: The array is free text and is not a controlled provenance vocabulary.

claims.text: The source's allele-origin strings.

purpose.text: Use datatypeId to group evidence by the release's broad evidence type.

purpose.text: Use score to compare evidence only within one source.

limitations.text: Do not compare scores across sources or with an aggregate association score. A constant score, such as 1.0 for reactome and cancer_biomarkers, ranks nothing.

claims.text: One Orphanet curation associating a gene with a rare disease.

purpose.text: Use id as the evidence record's node key.

limitations.text: Do not carry the id across releases: a changed input mints a new hash. The hash covers the row's identity fields, not its free text or score, unless the source's own definition says otherwise.

claims.text: The source row's id.

purpose.text: Use datasourceId to tell which source supplied the evidence.

limitations.text: The code is a reporting label; it does not encode the evidence method.

claims.text: The release's datasource code for the evidence row.

purpose.text: Use datatypeId to group evidence by the release's broad evidence type.

limitations.text: Two sources sharing a datatypeId are not measuring the same thing.

claims.text: The release's evidence-type bucket for the row.

purpose.text: Use score to compare evidence only within one source.

limitations.text: Do not compare scores across sources or with an aggregate association score. A constant score, such as 1.0 for reactome and cancer_biomarkers, ranks nothing.

claims.text: The release's per-row evidence score.
The score is already on the source's own scale. Its range and meaning differ by source and it is not a probability or a p-value.

purpose.text: Use resourceScore to read the source's native quantity for the row.

limitations.text: The native quantity and its scale differ by source. A null resourceScore means the source has no such column, not that the row scored zero.

claims.text: The source's native score where the dataset publishes one.

resourceScore is the source's own quantity (for example a raw literature mention count or a fine-mapping score), not a rescaled version of score. It is null on the eleven sources that do not publish one.

purpose.text: Use publicationDate to date the evidence by the earliest publication the source attaches to the row.
