limitations.text: A target with no protein edge is a gene for which the release lists no protein identifier; it is not evidence that the gene encodes no protein.
A protein identifier is not a structure, an isoform function or proof of expression. One gene can map to several protein identifiers, and a retired accession does not resolve to a current entry.

claims.text: A protein-record identifier listed for a target: a current UniProt accession, a retired UniProt accession, or an Ensembl protein id. It names a protein record, not the gene that encodes it.
(source, identifier), written source:identifier. One node per identifier in the namespace named by source.
source separates current UniProt entries from retired ones and from Ensembl protein ids. identifier is the accession as the release spells it; the same string under two sources is two identifiers.

purpose.text: Use it to place the interval on a chromosome and to group by chromosome.

limitations.text: Never null.
Not sortable numerically as text and not an Ensembl region name.

claims.text: GRCh38 chromosome label of the interval, without a chr prefix.
Categorical string; 1-22, X, Y and MT style labels as the release writes them.

purpose.text: Use it with end to bound the interval on GRCh38.

limitations.text: Never null.
One-based inclusive coordinates, not a BED half-open interval.

claims.text: Lowest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the interval.
Base pairs; always less than end. Interval length is 501-6,637 bp.

purpose.text: Base pairs; read with chromosome and start.

limitations.text: Never null.
One-based inclusive, not a BED end.

claims.text: Highest one-based GRCh38 coordinate of the interval.

purpose.text: Use it to select predictions by the model's interval class.

limitations.text: Never null.
A model label, not an ontology term and not a validated promoter or enhancer call.

claims.text: The E2G model's classification of where the interval sits relative to the linked gene.
Three values: promoter, genic, intergenic. Promoter rows always have distanceToTss 0.

purpose.text: Use it to rank element-gene links within one biosample.

limitations.text: Never null.
A within-model score, not a probability, an effect size or a validated interaction. Scores from different studies in the same biosample are separate predictions and are not merged by this node.

claims.text: The datasource's evidence score for the element-gene link; the release states that higher values indicate stronger support.
Continuous in [0.6, 1.0] in 26.09.

purpose.text: Use it to place the interval relative to the gene's TSS.

limitations.text: Never null.
Because the sign is absent, the value cannot tell an upstream from a downstream element; use the coordinates against the gene's strand.

claims.text: Distance in base pairs from the interval to the linked gene's transcription start site, as a non-negative magnitude.
0 for every promoter row; up to 55,760,344 for intergenic rows. No negative value occurs, so the sign is not in the data.

purpose.text: Use it to confirm the prediction came from the E2G datasource.

limitations.text: Never null.
The dataset has no other contributor, so the property carries no discrimination today.

claims.text: The release's datasource for the prediction.
One value in 26.09: E2G.

purpose.text: Use it to trace a prediction to the ENCODE experiment behind it.

limitations.text: Never null and never empty.
An ENCODE experiment accession is not an Open Targets studyId; it joins nothing in the genetics layer.

claims.text: The ENCODE accession of the experiment that produced the prediction.
1,439 distinct ENCFF accessions; up to 39,800 rows each.

purpose.text: Use it to name each element of resourceScoreValue by position.

limitations.text: A graph property cannot hold an array of structs, so the scores are split into two parallel arrays; resourceScoreName[i] belongs to resourceScoreValue[i] and neither array may be sorted alone.

claims.text: The component names of the model's resourceScore array, in array order.
Always exactly two elements in the order [DNase, HiC_contacts] on all 48,808,491 rows.

purpose.text: Use it to read the two resource scores by position.

limitations.text: Positional pairing with resourceScoreName is the only reading the release supports; the release does not state which component drives the link score.

claims.text: The values of the model's resourceScore array, in array order.
Two values per row and never null: DNase in [0.30001, 1.0], HiC_contacts in [0.000355, 0.95732].

purpose.text: Use it to check whether the source attached a QC flag.

limitations.text: Never null; present and empty.
An empty array records that no QC flag was attached, not that the prediction passed a threshold.

claims.text: The source's quality-control flags for the prediction.
An empty array on all 48,808,491 rows, so it never qualifies a node.

purpose.text: Use this node as the release's element-gene-study prediction record.

limitations.text: No node means no E2G prediction for that interval in this release.

The node is biosample- and study-specific: the same genomic interval and gene appear once per ENCODE study with the same coordinates and different scores, so counting nodes counts predictions, not elements. Nothing here is a measured enhancer-gene interaction, a variant effect or a disease mechanism.
Do not read the id count as the number of distinct regulatory elements; two nodes with the same coordinates are not two elements.

claims.text: A regulatory interval as the release's E2G model reports it for one biosample and one study, with the gene it is predicted to regulate. It is a prediction record, not a validated enhancer or promoter.

enhancer_to_gene.intervalId, a 32-hex-character hash: 48,808,491 rows carry 48,806,245 distinct ids, and the 2,246 repeated ids are exact duplicate rows. The id is not a genomic-interval id: 38,343,584 distinct (chromosome, start, end, biosampleId) intervals exist, and one interval linked to one gene recurs once per study (up to 255 times for one such interval). Read the node as the release's element-gene-study record.

chromosome, start and end are GRCh38 coordinates in the release's own spelling (no chr prefix). intervalType is the model's classification of the interval: promoter (24,407,590 rows), genic (13,257,251) or intergenic (11,143,650). score is the E2G link score; distanceToTss is a non-negative distance to the gene's TSS, zero for every promoter row. The gene is the REGULATES edge, the biosample and publication are separate edges.
A gene absent from this node set has no predicted element in the 322 covered biosamples.
Only 20,088 targets have any prediction and only 322 biosamples are covered.
An intervalId is one study's element-gene prediction.
48.8M ids are element-gene-study predictions, and only 38,343,584 distinct genomic intervals occur.

purpose.text: Use it to read the event as the datasource writes it.

limitations.text: Do not group by event text as if it were a MedDRA, HPO or EFO term. Identical strings from different datasources are not the same curated term; eventId is the accession where the source supplies one.

claims.text: The event text as the contributing datasource writes it.
Free text: 1,459 distinct strings over 4,387 rows. The labels mix clinical events, assay readouts and model-organism observations.

purpose.text: Use it to read the source's ontology accession for the event.

limitations.text: A null id is a source gap, not a claim that the event has no ontology term.
The accessions are not filtered to the release's disease vocabulary, and the event string is not checked against the accession's label.

claims.text: The ontology accession the source supplies for the event, in underscore form such as HP_0001649 or MONDO_0005252.
Null on 2,176 rows, mostly ToxCast and ClinPGx, which name an event without an accession.

Present on 2,211 of 4,387 rows over 435 distinct accessions from eight prefixes: MONDO, HP, EFO, GO, NCIT, CHEBI, MP and OBA. The prefixes mix diseases, phenotypes, biological processes, a chemical and model-organism terms. The build carries the accession as a property and does not resolve it to a DiseaseNode or GO term.

purpose.text: Use it to attribute an observation to the reporting datasource.

limitations.text: The values are not normalised across programmes or papers and do not name a release dataset. Two spellings of one source would be two datasources here.

claims.text: The source that contributed the observation: a program, a study or a paper, for example ClinPGx, ToxCast, AOP-Wiki or Lynch et al. (2017).
Nine values cover the 4,387 rows. ClinPGx (1,590) and Lynch et al. (2017) (1,341) supply most rows.

purpose.text: Use it to read the citation attached to an observation.

limitations.text: A null citation is a source gap, not an uncited finding.
One PMID can back hundreds of rows; the field does not say which part of the paper supports the observation.

claims.text: The PubMed id cited for the observation, as a decimal string.
Null on 2,446 rows, which record a source page or program instead of a paper.
Non-null on 1,941 rows over 5 distinct PMIDs; every value is numeric. It is a citation attached to the observation, not a PublicationNode edge in this layer.

purpose.text: Use it to reach the source page that records the observation.

limitations.text: A null url means the source supplied no page, not that no source exists.
A locator is not proof that the page supports the row. ToxCast reuses one page across many events and targets, so the url is not unique to an event.

claims.text: The source page recorded for the observation.
Non-null on 2,446 rows and null on 1,941. The value is also part of the node key, where null is written as the empty string.

purpose.text: Use this node as the datasource's safety observation for one target.

limitations.text: No node means the release records no such observation for that target. A null eventId, literature or url is a source gap, not an empty event, citation or page.

The node is the observation, not a controlled event vocabulary: the same event text from the same datasource for another target is a different node, and two datasources writing the same clinical event are not merged. Two nodes can therefore share every stored property and differ only by their incoming target edge. Effects and biosamples are separate edges. studies is a documented limit: a description/name/type triple is not an identified study, so it produces no node or edge and stays in the source. Nothing here asserts causality, incidence, severity or a dose-response.

claims.text: A safety observation row from target_safety_event: one datasource reporting that a target is associated with an event, with the source's event accession, citation and page where supplied.

targetId|event|datasource|eventId|url, with the empty string where eventId or url is null: 4,387 rows and 4,387 distinct keys. The target is part of the identity because each row is a target-specific observation, but it is not a property; the incoming HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edge carries it. (targetId, event, datasource) has only 4,337 distinct values, and adding eventId still gives 4,337: 31 repeated (target, event, datasource, eventId) groups, 15 of them with a null eventId, are separated only by url. eventId is null on 2,176 rows overall, and rows with both extra fields null still have distinct target, event and datasource triples.

studies has 5,561 elements forming 3,448 distinct description/name/type triples. name is null on 642 elements, carries an HP_, EFO_, MONDO_ or GO_ accession on 1,764, and free text (for example 'cyclophosphamide induced effect') on the rest; description is free text on 5,119; type is biochemical, cell-based, clinical or preclinical, with one null.

event is free text as the datasource writes it, not an ontology label. eventId, where present, is an accession in underscore form from several vocabularies (MONDO_, HP_, EFO_, GO_, NCIT_, CHEBI_, MP_, OBA_). datasource is the contributing source, not a release dataset. literature is a PubMed id as text. url is the source page.

purpose.text: Use direction to select observations by the reported direction of effect.

limitations.text: The wording combines activation, increase and upregulation into one bucket; it does not distinguish pharmacology from physiology.

claims.text: The signed direction of the reported effect.
Two values only: Activation/Increase/Upregulation (1,162 elements) and Inhibition/Decrease/Downregulation (1,187 elements).

purpose.text: Use dosing to select observations by the reported dosing context.

limitations.text: Null means the source states no dosing context, not that dosing was zero.
The values are coarse context labels, not doses, schedules or exposures, and they are not ordered by severity.

claims.text: The dosing context in which the effect was reported.
acute (1,286 elements), general (560), chronic (61), developmental toxicity (36) or null (406).

purpose.text: Use a safety-event effect node to identify the direction and dosing context reported for a safety observation.

limitations.text: No effect node means no effects element names the pair. A null dosing is a source gap, not a no-dose context.

The descriptor exists so that direction and dosing are not flattened into variable-length properties of the observation; it has no identity beyond the pair. direction describes the reported effect of modulating the target on the event, not the event's direction in a patient. dosing is a coarse context, not a dose, duration or exposure. The edge, not the node, ties a descriptor to an observation.
Do not read a descriptor as a curated ontology term: it is a source vocabulary label with no identity beyond the direction and dosing pair.

claims.text: An effect descriptor: the direction in which modulating the target is reported to change the event, together with the dosing context. It is a shared nine-value vocabulary, not an assay, study or measured effect.
direction|dosing, with the empty string where dosing is null: 9 distinct pairs over 2,349 array elements. direction is never null; dosing is null on 406 elements.
The nine descriptors are a closed vocabulary for this release.
direction is one of two statements: Activation/Increase/Upregulation or Inhibition/Decrease/Downregulation. dosing is acute, general, chronic or developmental toxicity, or null.

purpose.text: Use label as the term's display name; join on id.

limitations.text: Not a key: a label-to-id join can return two rows. One row carries the upstream placeholder '<new term>', which is a label but not a usable term name.

claims.text: The SO term name copied verbatim, words joined by underscores.
2,612 distinct labels cover 2,620 rows; 8 labels cover two accessions each. Two labels contain a space and are not spaced prose.

purpose.text: Use an SO term node to classify or group variants by consequence.

limitations.text: A term absent from so is outside the release's SO subset. No id or label is null.
The conversion from SO_ to SO: is required for every consequence join. A consequence edge names a predicted effect, not an observed functional assay.

claims.text: A Sequence Ontology term used to describe a variant consequence.
so.id, the SO accession in colon form: 2,620 rows and 2,620 distinct ids from SO:0000000 to SO:3000000.
The term names a consequence class; severity is not encoded by the term alone. Released consequence columns write the underscore form (SO_0001583), so a join must convert the separator.
All 7,886,761 non-null variant.mostSevereConsequenceId values resolve here after SO_ becomes SO:.

purpose.text: Choose the sample-size fields that apply to a study.

limitations.text: Never null; studies of unknown design are excluded upstream.
Not the full API enum and says nothing about trait, tissue or condition.

claims.text: Study design: gwas or one of five molecular QTL classes, eqtl, pqtl, sqtl, tuqtl or sceqtl.
Lower-case categorical code; it selects which other study fields are populated.

purpose.text: Read a study's trait as the source reported it, before the release's standardised mapping.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
Not the standardised trait; use traitFromSourceMappedIds for that.

claims.text: Trait exactly as the source reported it, from a disease name to an opaque molecular feature id.
Two kinds of value share the column, so read it with studyType.

purpose.text: Trace a study's metadata to the project that supplied it.

limitations.text: Never null in 26.09.
The project's vintage or assay version is not encoded; do not infer quality from it alone.

claims.text: Source project collection that supplied the study metadata.
Provenance handle, not an accession or a quality mark.

purpose.text: Identify the paper a study's metadata came from by its title.

limitations.text: Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata, not a missing study.
Coverage is GWAS-Catalog-only, so it is not a literature index for the whole release.

claims.text: Title of the publication referencing the study, where the source supplied one.
Raw title text that may still contain inline HTML.

purpose.text: Identify the paper a study's metadata came from by its first author.

limitations.text: Not a stable author identifier and not available for molecular studies.

claims.text: First author of the study's publication, as the source wrote it.
Surname and initials text with mixed ordering conventions.
Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata.

purpose.text: Date a study's publication for triage.

limitations.text: Not the study or evidence date; do not use it to compute novelty.

claims.text: Publication date of the study's paper, stored as YYYY-MM-DD text.
Sortable in this form; the range includes genuinely old and future-dated records.
Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata.

purpose.text: Identify the journal a study's paper appeared in.

limitations.text: One journal can have several abbreviations, and no journal entity exists to join.

claims.text: Abbreviated journal name where the study's publication appeared.
The source's own abbreviation, not a normalised journal name.
Null on studies without GWAS-Catalog publication metadata.

purpose.text: Read the source's description of a study's starting cohort.

limitations.text: Null when the source supplied no starting-cohort description.
Never parse it as the analysed sample size; use nSamples, nCases and nControls.

claims.text: Free-text account of the study's starting cohort, as reported by the source.
Human-readable string that may be a cross-reference rather than a count.

purpose.text: Size the case group of a case-control study.

limitations.text: Not an ancestry stratum; the interface may hide a genuine zero.

claims.text: Number of cases the study analysed, as a whole-study total.
Count; zero is a real value, and it is read with nControls.
Null on non-GWAS rows and on GWAS rows without case counts.

purpose.text: Size the control group of a case-control study.

limitations.text: Not an ancestry stratum and not derivable from nSamples.

claims.text: Number of controls the study analysed, as a whole-study total.
Count; zero is a real value, and it shares nulls with nCases.
Null on non-GWAS rows and on GWAS rows without control counts.

purpose.text: Read the analysed sample total of a study.

limitations.text: Null on a few GWAS rows where the source supplied no analysed total, not a zero-sample study.
It can be smaller than nCases plus nControls on some rows; never derive one from the others.

claims.text: Total number of samples tested in the study analysis.
Count; the analysed total, not a case-control sum.

purpose.text: Decide whether to follow a study's summary-statistics location.

limitations.text: Null only for studies split from one catalogue accession, where availability was never asserted.
True does not mean the statistics are analysable or that the study can be fine-mapped.

claims.text: Whether the source publishes summary statistics for the study.
Boolean; true is a precondition for a statistics location and QC, not a usability guarantee.

purpose.text: Locate a study's published summary statistics.

limitations.text: Null when the release carried no source path, including many GWAS Catalog studies that do have statistics.
Not evidence that statistics are unavailable; read it with hasSumstats.

claims.text: Path or URL where the source publishes the study's summary statistics.
Free-text URI whose scheme names the host.

purpose.text: Compare molecular-QTL studies by experimental condition.

limitations.text: Null on GWAS rows and some pQTL rows, where the design has no condition rather than a missing value.
No controlled vocabulary; do not treat the same label from two projects as the same experiment.

claims.text: Experimental condition of a molecular-QTL study, in the source's own label.
Categorical stimulus and exposure shorthand; '+' marks combined stimulation and 'naive' means unstimulated.

purpose.text: Qualify the evidence the release reports by the study behind it: its design, sample size and publication.

limitations.text: A null sample size or ancestry is missing release metadata, not a zero-sample study. A study absent here is outside the release.
A study is not a publication: several studies can share one PMID, and a study can have no PMID. Do not treat the study id as a publication id.

claims.text: One study record: a GWAS, eQTL, pQTL, sQTL or other molecular QTL analysis. A study is the unit that carries sample size, ancestry, publication metadata and the disease or trait it measures.
study.studyId. The id is unique in the release; a molecular QTL study is split by its target trait and biosample, so it is not the same unit as a publication.
studyType separates GWAS from molecular QTL types. nCases/nControls apply to case-control designs; nSamples is the general sample count.

purpose.text: Use location as the free-text localisation statement.

limitations.text: The release's subcellularLocations array never carries a null location.
Do not compare the free-text location with the ontology label in labelSL: the same free-text location can differ from that label.

claims.text: The localisation statement as free text, including topology and membrane-pass qualifiers.
The string is not an accession; join to the ontology through termSL when a normalized term is needed.
First component of the node key.

purpose.text: Use source to know which resource reported the localisation statement.

limitations.text: The release's subcellularLocations array never carries a null source.
The resource is not a confidence level; the release supplies no score.

claims.text: The resource that reported the localisation statement.
One component of the node key.
Observed values are uniprot, HPA_main, HPA_additional and HPA_extracellular_location.

purpose.text: Use termSL to join the statement to the subcellular-location ontology.

limitations.text: Null when the release did not map the statement to an ontology term.
A shared termSL does not make two statements the same localisation.

claims.text: The subcellular-location ontology accession assigned to the statement.
One component of the node key.
termSL is often a broad term such as a cellular-component class while location carries the specific text.

purpose.text: Read labelSL as the ontology label of termSL, not as a normalized form of location.

limitations.text: The label repeats across distinct free-text locations; do not group by it.

claims.text: The label of the ontology term named by termSL.
One component of the node key.
Null when termSL is null.

purpose.text: Read targetModifier to see whether the statement is restricted to an isoform.

limitations.text: Null means the statement is not isoform-restricted in the release; it does not mean every isoform was tested.
The modifier is a release string, not a transcript or protein accession.

claims.text: The isoform qualifier the release attaches to the localisation, for example Isoform 2.
One component of the node key.
Most statements have no modifier and apply to the gene product generally.

purpose.text: Use a subcellular-location node to identify a localisation statement reported for a target.

limitations.text: A target with no location edge has no localisation statement in the release; it is not evidence that the protein has no location.
Localisation is a reported observation, not a measurement made by this release. A free-text location can include membrane-pass and topology qualifiers that termSL does not capture.

claims.text: A localisation statement reported for a target by UniProt or the Human Protein Atlas. The node is the statement, including its free-text topology qualifier and any isoform restriction.

subcellular_location::location::source::termSL::labelSL::targetModifier, with the empty string for a null component. The same location is reported by several sources and isoforms, so the source and modifiers are part of the identity.
location is the free-text statement; termSL and labelSL map it to the release's subcellular-location ontology. targetModifier names an isoform when the statement applies to one isoform only.

purpose.text: Use label to compare a target synonym string exactly.

limitations.text: The release's three synonym arrays never carry a null label.
Two targets can share a label; the node is a vocabulary entry, not a target.

claims.text: The synonym string as the release spells it.
Last component of the node key.
Case and punctuation are as supplied; there is no normalization.

purpose.text: Use kind to select which synonym array supplied the string.

limitations.text: The kinds are release fields, not an ontology of synonym scopes.

claims.text: The synonym array that supplied the string.
One component of the node key.
Every synonym node names one kind.
synonym is the general synonym list, symbolSynonym an alternative gene symbol and nameSynonym an alternative gene name.

purpose.text: Use source with kind and label to identify the synonym.

limitations.text: The release's three synonym arrays never carry a null source.
The source is not a confidence or an indication that the name is official.

claims.text: The vocabulary that supplied the synonym.
One component of the node key.
Observed values are HGNC, uniprot and NCBI_entrez.

purpose.text: Use a synonym node to match an alternative target name to its kind and source.

limitations.text: A synonym absent here was not listed for any target in the release; it may still be an accepted name elsewhere.
A synonym is a naming fact. It does not mean the string is approved, current or unique to one target; obsolete symbols are a separate field.

claims.text: A name or symbol the release lists for a target, qualified by the kind of synonym array it came from and the vocabulary that supplied it.
synonym::kind::source::label. The same string can occur in several kinds or sources and remains a distinct node.
kind is the array that carried the string: synonym, symbolSynonym or nameSynonym. source names the vocabulary (HGNC, uniprot, NCBI_entrez).

purpose.text: Use id with label and level to identify a target-class node.

limitations.text: The release's targetClass array never carries a null id.
The id is internal to the release and is not an ontology accession.
The same id appears at several levels with different labels, so it must not be used as a class identifier on its own.

claims.text: The release's numeric identifier for a target-class node.
One component of the node key, with label and level.

purpose.text: Read the label together with level; the same label can recur at other levels.

limitations.text: The release's targetClass array never carries a null label.
A label is not unique across levels or releases; do not join on it alone.

claims.text: The class name at this hierarchy level.
One component of the node key.

purpose.text: Use level with label and id to identify a class and compare its depth.

limitations.text: The release's targetClass array never carries a null level.
The tiers are the release's own depth labels, not ontology ranks.

claims.text: The hierarchy tier of the class, written l1 to l6.
One component of the node key.
l1 is the root tier; higher numbers are more specific classes.

purpose.text: Use a target-class node to place a target in the release's classification hierarchy.

limitations.text: A target with no class edge is unclassified in the release, not classless in biology.
The classification is a curated descriptor for target assessment. It is not a functional assay, a protein family membership proof or a drug tractability claim.

claims.text: A node in the release's target-classification tree: a class label at one hierarchy level, with the release's numeric class id.
target_class::id::label::level. The numeric id is reused across levels with different labels, so the id alone is not the identity.
level is the hierarchy tier (l1 to l6). A gene carries one edge per ancestor class from the most specific tier up to the root.

purpose.text: Use modality with category to select one tractability assessment axis.

limitations.text: The codes are abbreviations whose expansions the release does not define in this dataset; do not infer them from the letters.

claims.text: The drug-modality code the assessment applies to.

purpose.text: Use category with modality to select one tractability evidence axis.

limitations.text: Labels are free-text source names, not a controlled vocabulary: 'High-Quality Pocket' and 'Med-Quality Pocket' are separate buckets, and a bucket does not imply the others.

claims.text: The tractability evidence axis the assessment applies to.
Nineteen labels such as Approved Drug, Phase 1 Clinical, High-Quality Pocket, High-Quality Ligand and UniProt loc high conf. Each label is reported under a subset of the four modalities.

purpose.text: Use a tractability bucket node to select one modality-by-category assessment axis.

limitations.text: A bucket absent here is not an assessment axis in this release.

The release does not expand the modality codes in this dataset; do not read AB, SM, PR or OC as a spelled-out modality without external documentation. Bucket names are source labels, not a hierarchy, and they mix structural, localisation, ligand and clinical evidence.
Do not read the bucket as a measured property of a target; it names one assessment axis, and the yes/no value is carried by the target's edge.

claims.text: A tractability bucket: one (modality, category) axis on which the release reports a yes/no assessment for a target.
modality|category: 28 buckets over 4 modality codes and 19 categories. Every one of the 18,869 assessed targets has exactly one row per bucket, 528,332 rows in total.
The bucket node exists so the modality and category vocabulary is shared instead of repeated on 528,332 edges.
modality is the source code as written: AB, SM, PR, OC. category names the evidence axis, for example High-Quality Pocket, Approved Drug or UniProt loc high conf.

purpose.text: Use biotype to select coding or non-coding transcripts.

limitations.text: The label is the release's biotype vocabulary, not a functional assay.

claims.text: The transcript biotype from the release's annotation.
protein_coding (278,455 rows) separates coding transcripts from lncRNA, nonsense_mediated_decay and other non-coding biotypes.

purpose.text: Read it together with biotype; a non-coding transcript has no translation.

limitations.text: A null proteinId is the release's annotation, not a zero-length protein.
The identifier names a translation, not a UniProt entry or a folded structure.

claims.text: The ENSP translation identifier of the transcript.
proteinId is null for 273,406 of 644,292 transcripts.

purpose.text: Use the flag to select the Ensembl canonical transcript of a target.

limitations.text: Canonical is an annotation choice; it does not establish expression, dominance or clinical relevance.

claims.text: Whether the release marks the transcript as the Ensembl canonical transcript of its gene.
True on 78,733 transcripts, exactly one per target gene.

purpose.text: Compare chromosome with the target's chromosome.

claims.text: The chromosome of the transcript's genomic span.
A transcript lies on the gene's chromosome in this release.

purpose.text: Use start with end and strand to locate the transcript span.

limitations.text: Do not compare them with another assembly without a liftover.

claims.text: The transcript span's start coordinate on the chromosome.
Coordinates are the release's chromosome coordinates; strand tells the direction.

purpose.text: Use end with start to locate the transcript span.

claims.text: The transcript span's end coordinate on the chromosome.
start/end describe the transcript, not the encoded protein.

purpose.text: Use strand with start and end to orient the transcript span.

claims.text: The transcript's strand, 1 for forward and -1 for reverse.

110,940,745 edges. Null statistics are release gaps: logBF is null on 24,500,428 rows, beta on 23,813,059, standardError on 15,809,462, the p-value on 32,391,750 and r2Overall on 86,440,317.

claims.text: One edge per direct is-a parent; several parents are GO's multiple inheritance. 38,089 live terms have at least one is-a parent and 3 live terms are roots. Every parent resolves to a go row, no term is its own parent, and no is-a edge crosses namespace.

child go.id and parent go.id joined by '|': 57,456 edges with 57,456 distinct pairs.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read a GO term's negative regulation target.

limitations.text: Inhibition is not the complement of activation, so one direction does not imply the other.

The sign is in the edge type, not in the target value. Every regulated term resolves to a live go row and 73 edges cross namespaces.

regulator go.id and regulated go.id joined by '|': 2,624 edges over 2,620 regulator terms, with unique pairs.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read a GO term's direct part-of parent.

claims.text: Direct part-of parents only; 41,727 of 48,340 rows hold an empty array, which is normal for molecular-function terms. Every parent resolves to a go row and no term is its own parent. 786 edges (11.1%) join terms from different namespaces.

child go.id and parent go.id joined by '|': 7,058 edges over 6,613 child terms, with unique pairs.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read a GO term's positive regulation target.

regulator go.id and regulated go.id joined by '|': 2,627 edges over 2,626 regulator terms, with unique pairs.

regulator go.id and regulated go.id joined by '|': 2,939 edges with 2,939 distinct pairs.

purpose.text: Use this value as the pair's maximum clinical stage.

claims.text: The best-ranked stage among the pair's contributing reports, with WITHDRAWAL and PHASE_4 folded into APPROVAL.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read the release's clinical-development roll-up for a drug-disease pair.

limitations.text: No edge means the release formed no pair. Reports flagged PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED or INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE were excluded before pairs were formed, so absence is not a negative clinical finding.

A pair is not a trial and not an approval: APPROVAL means approval-status evidence from any report family. The contributing report ids are not materialised as edges; a report already names its own drugs and diseases and the roll-up is QC-filtered, so it is not reproducible from them.

claims.text: The release reports clinical development of the molecule in the disease, rolled up over the reports that name both. One edge per drug-disease pair in clinical_indication.

The release also lists the contributing report ids (321,785 pair-report memberships, all resolving in clinical_report.id); 11,948 of 86,451 pairs differ from a report-array reconstruction.

maxClinicalStage is the best rank among the pair's contributing reports, with WITHDRAWAL and PHASE_4 folded into APPROVAL and UNKNOWN kept as a published value. It is not the stage of the latest or largest trial.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read the release's drug-target pair with clinical reports naming the drug.

limitations.text: A pair missing here has no mechanism target in the release's mechanism table, or its drug had no QC-passing report: reports flagged PHASE_IV_NOT_APPROVED, UNVALIDATED_INDICATION or INDIRECT_PRIMARY_PURPOSE are dropped.

(drugId, targetId). The row's id is a hash of the pair.
The source row's diseases array and clinicalReportIds are per-drug roll-ups; its 54,648 drug-disease pairs are a subset of HAS_CLINICAL_INDICATION pairs and add no pair.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read an external identifier the release lists for a molecule.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such identifier for the molecule.

A listed identifier is not a verified identity: two molecules citing the same cross-reference are not thereby the same molecule, and the release does not re-resolve the external record. Source spellings are not normalised across datasets, so the same authority can appear as drugbank here and DrugBank on a target.

(drug_molecule.id, crossReferences.source, crossReferences.ids element).
The edge points at a shared CrossReferenceNode keyed source:identifier. source is the authority (drugbank, Probes&Drugs), not the entity type.

limitations.text: No edge means no warning row names the molecule.

The edge says the warning names the molecule, not that the molecule caused the effect. Five chemblIds in drug_warning are absent from the molecule rows, so those edges point outside the molecule node set.

(drug_warning.chemblIds element, drug_warning.id).
Country, warning type, year and disease context are on the warning node.

limitations.text: Do not read the vocabulary as a pharmacodynamic ontology: it is source-controlled and mixes pharmacodynamic and modality terms.

Direction is not implied by mechanismOfAction text.

(chemblId, target Ensembl id, actionType, mechanismOfAction, targetName, targetType). The tuple is unique across the 14,718 expanded molecule-target pairs, so rows with identical mechanism text stay distinct.

limitations.text: No edge means parentId is null, not that the molecule has no chemical parent.

purpose.text: Read this edge from a molecule to a synonym name.

limitations.text: No edge means no synonym with a usable label and source. The molecule's preferred name is not a synonym edge.

(drug_molecule.id, synonyms.source, synonyms.label).
The name node carries the string and its authority; this edge says the release classified the pair as a synonym.

purpose.text: Read this edge from a molecule to a trade name.

limitations.text: No edge means no trade name with a usable label and source.
A trade name is a product label, not an approval, an indication or a statement that the molecule is marketed in a jurisdiction.

claims.text: The molecule has a product name that the release records as a trade name.
(drug_molecule.id, tradeNames.source, tradeNames.label).
A trade name labels a marketed product; it is not the active ingredient's preferred name.

purpose.text: Use it to read the MP phenotype observed in a mouse model.

limitations.text: No edge means the model has no recorded MP phenotype; none occur.

The observation is a curated MP term for one model in one genetic background, not a measured effect size. MP and HP terms are different vocabularies and are not merged, so this edge never reaches an HPO term.

claims.text: The mouse model was observed with this Mammalian Phenotype term. The term is the observation on the row, not a class of the model.
biologicalModels.id|HAS_PHENOTYPE|modelPhenotypeId: 243,341 distinct model-phenotype pairs over the 256,254 model entries. Repeated rows collapse to one edge.

modelPhenotypeId is an MP accession in colon form and is never null; 10,584 distinct terms occur and each has a PhenotypeNode from the evidence layer. modelPhenotypeLabel is the term's label on the same row and is not stored, because the term's node carries it.

purpose.text: Use it to read the source's class of an observed phenotype.

limitations.text: No edge means the row records no class for its phenotype; none occur.

The class is the source's broad system label, not an ontology parent walk: the release publishes no MP hierarchy, so an IS_A edge between the observed term and its class does not exist. The class does not add a phenotype beyond the observation.

claims.text: The model's phenotype belongs to this MP class term, the system-level category the source records alongside the observation (for example nervous system phenotype). It is a classification of the observed phenotype, not a second observation.
biologicalModels.id|HAS_PHENOTYPE_CLASS|modelPhenotypeClasses.id: 127,802 distinct model-class pairs from 344,055 model-element and class-element combinations over the 28 class terms.

A closed 28-term vocabulary (MP:0001186 pigmentation phenotype, MP:0005367 renal/urinary system phenotype, ...). 60,824 of the 203,583 rows carry more than one class, up to five. 21 of the 28 class terms also occur as observations; 7 occur only here, so this edge is their only binding.

purpose.text: Use it to read the publications a model's record cites.

limitations.text: No edge means the model entry cites no PMID or cites one outside the release's literature corpus. 96 model ids carry more than one distinct literature array across their rows.
The edge says the model record cites the paper, not that the paper reports this phenotype. It is not the IMPC evidence citation, which lives on the IMPC evidence node.

claims.text: A publication cited on the model's biologicalModels entry. The release stores literature as a PMID array per model entry; the graph models it as an edge rather than a string array property.

biologicalModels.id|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 130,911 distinct model-pmid pairs from 1,249,431 PMID elements and 24,380 distinct pmids; a model cited by several phenotype rows repeats its PMIDs and collapses.

Derived from a 1:1-consistent release field: the array holds 1-8 PMIDs on 215,502 model entries and is null on 40,752. 23,437 of the 24,380 distinct PMIDs resolve to a PublicationNode; the remaining 943 leave a dangling endpoint.

purpose.text: Use this value as the drug name ClinPGx writes for the edge.

limitations.text: A name, not a key: never join on it, and it can be a metabolite (n-desmethyltamoxifen).

claims.text: 1-3 names per row; 660 distinct names for 532 ChEMBL ids.
The drug name as ClinPGx writes it.
The 33,707 drug elements in 26.09 never carry a null.

purpose.text: Read annotation -> molecule.

limitations.text: A drug element with no drugId emits no edge, because a MoleculeNode is a ChEMBL molecule. No row has an empty drugs array.
The edge names the drug the response was observed with, not an indication, a dose or an approval. A drug absent from ChEMBL stays a name in the source rather than becoming a graph node.

claims.text: 4,094 array elements on 4,088 rows carry no drugId.
The edge carries drugFromSource, the name ClinPGx uses; drugId is the release's ChEMBL id. 660 names map to 532 ChEMBL ids.
A drug the annotation concerns, one edge per element of the row's drugs array. A multi-drug annotation keeps one row and therefore several edges.

annotation key|HAS_DRUG|drugId: 29,613 edges over the 29,391 rows that name a ChEMBL id. 29,328 resolve to drug_molecule.id and 285 dangle on three ChEMBL ids the molecule table does not hold (CHEMBL4525767, CHEMBL170365, CHEMBL501680).

purpose.text: Read annotation -> disease term.

limitations.text: No edge means the phrase matched no disease label.

The mapping is the release's label lookup, not ClinPGx's own disease assignment and not a diagnosis. It is sparse and many-to-one, so absence is not a healthy outcome and presence is not an established association.
A HAS_MAPPED_PHENOTYPE edge records a matched ontology term.
A pharmacogenomic annotation with a disease term is evidence that the genotype causes or treats that disease.

claims.text: No edge for 32,755 rows (97.8%); phenotypeText is still present on 31,625 of those rows.
MONDO_0018493 carries 581 of the 724 edges; the rest spread over 29 terms in MONDO, EFO, GO, HP and NCIT.
The disease or phenotype term the release matched to the annotation's phenotype phrase.
annotation key|HAS_MAPPED_PHENOTYPE|phenotypeFromSourceId: 724 edges, all resolving to disease.id; 30 distinct terms.

purpose.text: Read annotation -> target.

limitations.text: No edge means targetFromSourceId is null. A dangling edge means the release named an Ensembl gene that is not in its target universe; that is a resolution gap, not a different gene.

The binding cannot look up the target table, so it emits the edge for every non-null id and reports the 51 unresolved ids instead of silently dropping or inventing a target. The edge is annotation context, not evidence that the drug acts on the gene in patients.

claims.text: targetFromSourceId is null on 1,569 rows.
The gene id is the release's resolved Ensembl id, so it needs no symbol mapping. isDirectTarget on the node says whether the gene is a mechanism-of-action target of a row drug.
The gene the annotation says the genotype acts through.
annotation key|HAS_TARGET|targetFromSourceId: 31,910 edges, one per row with a gene id. 25,295 edges end at a TargetNode; 6,615 dangle on 51 Ensembl ids the target table does not hold.

purpose.text: Read annotation -> variant.

limitations.text: No edge means the row has no variantId. It does not mean the annotation is not about a variant.
variantRsId is not used as a fallback, because nothing in the release is keyed by rsID. The edge is the build's derived variant, not necessarily the allele the clinician annotated.

claims.text: 17,310 rows (51.7%) have no variantId: the 9,548 haplotype-anchored rows and 7,762 rsID-anchored genotypes that reduce to the reference.
14 of the 2,843 rsIDs resolve to no variant row.
The 16,169 edges cover 48.3% of the rows; the other 17,310 rows state no variantId.
The release variant the annotation is about: the variantId derived from the row's genotype. The edge exists only for rows that yield a single resolvable variant.
annotation key|HAS_VARIANT|variantId: 16,169 edges, one per row with a non-null variantId; all 2,882 distinct ids resolve to variant.variantId.

purpose.text: Read annotation -> paper.

limitations.text: No edge would mean the row cites nothing; that does not occur in 26.09. A dangling edge means the release cites a paper outside its text-mined publication corpus.
The citation is for the whole annotation, not for one genotype, drug or phenotype row, so edges repeat the same paper across the annotation's rows. Citing a paper is not a verification of its claim.

claims.text: literature is never null or empty and is sorted and de-duplicated by the writer; 5,952 distinct PMIDs back the 5,190 annotations.
A publication the annotation cites, one edge per element of the row's literature array.
annotation key|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 140,757 edges; 135,223 end at a PublicationNode and 5,534 dangle on 220 PubMed ids absent from literature_entity_lut. No pair repeats within a row.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read an external identifier listed by a phenotype term.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such identifier for the term.

A listed identifier is not verification of the external record and does not merge two phenotype terms. The node type is shared with the target and disease domains, so a shared identifier is one node with several inbound edges.

claims.text: Identifiers come from FMA, CALOHA, MESH, GO, BTO, EMAPA, UBERON and other anatomy and cell-ontology namespaces; every value carries a colon.
The phenotype term's record lists the external identifier.
phenotype -> source:identifier, keyed phenotype::accession::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier. The 43,966 elements are 43,966 distinct pairs within a term.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read a retired accession listed by a phenotype term.

limitations.text: No edge means the term lists no retired accession.
The edge preserves a historical accession without a successor link; it is not a synonym edge and does not merge terms.

claims.text: 297 of the elements are disease.id values, but they are listed as retired accessions of a phenotype term, so they resolve to ObsoleteTermNode and not to the DISEASE node with the same string.
The phenotype term lists the accession as one it has retired.
phenotype -> accession, keyed phenotype::accession::HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM::accession. The 5,955 elements are 5,955 distinct pairs; none is a disease_hpo.id.

limitations.text: Subtype does not imply that every annotation of the parent applies to the child.

claims.text: Direct parent edges; ancestors are reachable transitively.
The child phenotype term is a subtype of the parent term.
child accession -> parent accession.

purpose.text: Use this value to rank mentions within their own paper.

claims.text: Observed 0.01 to 1.510077108820886 in 26.09, median 0.675. It is neither a share nor a probability and passes 1; a mention in a high-weight early section outranks repeated late mentions.

A text match is not the paper's stance: the paper may support, dispute or only mention the entity. Every grounded pair is emitted with no relevance cutoff, so a mention count counts matched papers, not supporting findings.
The LUT carries variant, pathway or phenotype mentions under another keywordType.

One entity mention that the release's literature matcher grounded in one publication. The edge exists per publication, entity class and grounded identifier; it records the text match, not the paper's use of the entity.

(pmid, keywordType, keywordId). literature_entity_lut is unique on (pmid, keywordId) — 173,137,629 rows and no duplicate pair in 26.09 — and every keywordId belongs to one keywordType, so the triple is the row identity. Edges are keyed pmid::<class>::keywordId.
26.09 has exactly three keyword classes, DS disease or syndrome, GP gene or protein and CD chemical or drug; there is no variant, pathway, phenotype or anatomy mention class.

A disease mention is not an association, a diagnosis or a claim by the paper; it may be background, a comorbidity list or a negation. A phenotype, anatomy or process term reached by this edge is not a disease.

limitations.text: No edge means no ChEMBL identifier was grounded in this paper; it does not mean the paper does not discuss the drug.

The release's within-paper relevance of this grounded mention: a harmonic sum of section weights, each weight divided by its section rank squared, over the sections that mentioned the entity.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read a gene or protein the publication's text mentions.

limitations.text: No edge means no Ensembl gene identifier was grounded in this paper; a paper that names the gene by a symbol the matcher did not map is missed.
A mention of a gene is not the paper's finding about it and not experimental evidence for any association; a target named only as a control or in a citation list still gets an edge.

The publication's text mentions a gene or protein: a GP keyword grounded to target.id.
(pmid, 'GP', keywordId), with keywordId equal to target.id. All 55,952,088 GP pairs resolve to target.id (30,464 distinct Ensembl genes); every GP identifier is an ENSG accession.

purpose.text: Use it to walk a pathway's direct parents and children.

limitations.text: ancestors, descendants and path stay in reactome and are not edges. ancestors and descendants are transitive closures that repeat what this walk already gives; path is an ordered route (up to 11 per row, 75 rows with more than one root) whose canonical order is a build choice, not a relation. To get ancestry, walk this edge. Pathway membership is not a target-disease assertion.

claims.text: The child pathway is part of the direct parent pathway.
child reactome.id and parent reactome.id joined by '|': 2,899 edges with 2,899 distinct pairs.
2,854 pathways have at least one parent, 29 are roots, and a pathway has up to 6 parents. The parents and children arrays are exact inverses here: every parent element has its reverse child element.

purpose.text: Use it to read the biosample a prediction was made in.

limitations.text: No edge means the prediction names no biosample; none occur.
Activity in a biosample is the prediction's assay context, not measured chromatin state in a sample. biosampleFromSourceId is null on every row, so the source offers no finer sample identity.

claims.text: The regulatory element was predicted in this biosample, so the interval's activity is asserted for that tissue or cell type only.
intervalId|ACTIVE_IN|biosampleId: 48,806,245 edges, 1:1 with the element node.
All 322 distinct biosampleId values resolve to a BiosampleNode, and biosampleName is the label on the same row. The same genomic interval recurs in other biosamples as a different intervalId.

purpose.text: Use it to read the gene an element-gene prediction links to.

limitations.text: No edge means no predicted link. Every element node has one, so the edge carries no information beyond the node; it exists to attach the prediction to the target.

REGULATES states the model's prediction, not a measured regulatory effect, and it is not a target-disease assertion. The gene is the nearest or linked gene in the source's model, and one interval is predicted to regulate up to 20 genes.
The element does not regulate the gene in vivo, and modulating the element is not shown to change the target's expression.

claims.text: The E2G model predicts that this regulatory interval regulates this gene. The direction is element -> target, matching the ontology regulation edges; the source row is gene-anchored.
intervalId|REGULATES|geneId: 48,806,245 edges. intervalId determines geneId in every row, so the edge is 1:1 with the node.

All 20,088 distinct geneId values resolve to a TargetNode, so the binding leaves no dangling endpoint. score, distanceToTss and intervalType on the node qualify this link; the edge adds no property because it has exactly one object per node.
The edge records an E2G prediction.

purpose.text: Use it to read the publication the E2G predictions cite.

limitations.text: No edge means the row names no PMID; none occur.

The edge records the dataset's citation, not per-element experimental support: it adds 48.8M identical edges and no discrimination. Filter by datasourceId or start from the publication node instead of traversing it per element.

claims.text: The publication cited on an E2G prediction row.
intervalId|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid: 48,806,245 edges. pmid is the single value 38014075 on every row.
38014075 resolves to a PublicationNode, so the edge leaves no dangling endpoint. Because the value is constant, every element points at the same paper.

purpose.text: Read observation -> descriptor.

limitations.text: No edge means effects is null or empty. The observation still exists without an effect statement.
The edge does not rank the two effects of a row or state a mechanism. direction is source wording, not signed pharmacology or clinical benefit.

claims.text: The safety observation reports the direction-and-dosing descriptor.
effects is null on 2,073 rows.
safety event key|HAS_EFFECT|direction|dosing: 2,349 edges, unique per observation and descriptor.
2,314 rows carry effects; 35 of them carry two, which produce two edges.

purpose.text: Use it to read the tissue an observation was reported in.

limitations.text: No edge means the observation names no tissue.

Only tissueId becomes an edge; no cell-line or cell-type node is created from this array. The source tissueLabel is not carried: the node's name is the vocabulary label and can differ (UBERON_0004535 is 'cardiovascular' in the source and 'cardiovascular system' in biosample).

claims.text: The safety observation is reported in the tissue named by one biosample entry.
safety event key|OBSERVED_IN|normalised tissueId: 5,072 edges over the 2,601 observations that name a tissue, unique per observation and tissue.

The entry's tissueId is converted from colon to underscore form (31 elements write UBERON:...), which makes all 5,072 non-null tissue ids name a BiosampleNode. An observation can list up to six tissues, so the edge count exceeds the observation count.
438 biosample elements are cell-only and carry no tissueId.
cellId is null on all 5,599 elements; 438 elements carry only a cellFormat and 271 a cellLabel (mostly cell lines such as HepaRG and HepG2), and they produce no edge.

purpose.text: Navigate from a study to the credible sets it produced.

limitations.text: The edge does not assert that the study's trait is caused by any variant in the set.

claims.text: The credible set belongs to the study that produced it.
A study can have several credible sets; the set carries the locus.
studyId -> studyLocusId.

purpose.text: Place a molecular-QTL study in the biosample where it was measured.

limitations.text: A GWAS study has no MEASURED_IN edge; it has no molecular assay context here.
The edge is coarse: a measurement in a biosample is not evidence that the target is expressed there in every condition.

claims.text: The biosample in which the study's molecular measurement was made.
biosampleId is present on every QTL row and null on all GWAS rows. The biosample node's ontology ancestry, not this edge, separates tissue from cell type.
(studyId, biosampleId). 2,838,730 edges over 128 biosamples; every biosampleId resolves to biosample.biosampleId and 0 keys duplicate.
128 distinct biosamples cover all QTL studies.

purpose.text: Identify the gene a molecular-QTL study measures.

limitations.text: A GWAS study has no MEASURES_TARGET edge; it measures a trait, not a gene.
The edge names the measured gene, not a target-disease association and not a drug target. A QTL study can have several credible sets but only one measured target here.

claims.text: The target gene the study measures. On a molecular QTL this is the gene whose expression, splicing, transcript usage or protein level is the trait.
geneId is present on every QTL row (eqtl, sqtl, tuqtl, sceqtl, pqtl) and null on all 165,517 GWAS rows.
(studyId, geneId). 2,838,730 edges; every geneId resolves to target.id and 0 keys duplicate.

purpose.text: Trace a study record to the publication it cites.

limitations.text: A study with a null pubmedId has no edge.

One citation can back thousands of study records, so edge counts do not count papers. The edge is complete for the study table but not for the publication node set: an edge can name a PMID with no PublicationNode.

claims.text: A study record's cited publication, taken from the study's own PubMed reference.

The publication node carries the release's date, year and pmcid for the paper. The study keeps its own publicationTitle, journal and publicationDate copies. Every study pubmedId is a numeric PubMed number, so it can only match the numeric subset of the LUT keys.
(studyId, pubmedId). A study carries at most one pubmedId; several studies, above all the gene-by-biosample molecular-QTL rows, can share one publication.
2,953 of the 3,004,247 study rows in 26.09 carry a null pubmedId.

7,529 of the 7,703 distinct study PMIDs (893,960 of 3,001,294 rows with a PMID) occur in literature_entity_lut; the other 174 PMIDs (2,107,334 rows, mostly three large QTL papers) are cited by the release but absent from its text-mined corpus, so their edges name a publication key with no PublicationNode.

purpose.text: Read the trait the release annotates a study with.

limitations.text: A QTL study has no STUDIES_DISEASE edge; that is the release's shape and does not mean its trait is uncurated.
A study-trait annotation is the release's mapping of traitFromSource, not a diagnosis. A mapped id is not a verified equivalence between two ontology terms.

claims.text: A disease or trait term the study is annotated with.
diseaseIds holds the release's mapped trait terms. Molecular QTL study rows carry an empty array and therefore no edge.
(studyId, diseaseId). 194,151 edges from 165,517 GWAS studies; 0 duplicates and every disease id resolves to disease.id.

purpose.text: Compare direct association scores across target-disease pairs.

limitations.text: Never null; zero means no scored contribution, not necessarily no evidence.
Not comparable with indirect or per-source scores; the weighting is release-specific.

claims.text: Weighted harmonic aggregate of all direct evidence for the target-disease pair, up to the release.
Unitless value from 0 upward but below 1; higher means more or stronger accumulated direct evidence, not probability.

purpose.text: Compare the volume of evidence rows behind direct associations.

limitations.text: Null on the 53 rows whose series has no release-year element; never zero where present.
