purpose.text: Read target -> biosample for a baseline expression measurement.

limitations.text: No edge means the release carries no baseline measurement for that target in that context in any of the four sources. A null specificity_score is the source not computing it, not a specificity of zero. A null median means the distribution was not summarised.

One edge per target+tissue+celltype is not possible: a single triple-keyed edge would have to pick one and drop the rest. targetFromSourceId is not carried; every targetId resolves to a TargetNode. qualityControls is an empty array on every row, so it qualifies nothing. distribution_score and specificity_score are source scores in [0,1]; they are not probabilities and are not comparable with the Target Engine's tissue specificity on the PRIORITISATION_PROFILE.
The target is not necessarily expressed in that tissue in health or disease, not necessarily in every cell of the class, and not at the level the median states.
TPM, CPM and iBAQ values cannot be ranked or averaged together, and a bulk tissue value is not comparable with a single-cell value.
unit separates the measurement scales and must be read before comparing any two edges.

claims.text: A baseline expression measurement: one datasource's distribution of this target's transcript or protein abundance in a tissue and/or cell type. The edge is the measurement, not a statement that the target is expressed in every cell of that class.

targetId|EXPRESSED_IN|tissueBiosampleId|celltypeBiosampleId|datasourceId|tissueBiosampleFromSource|celltypeBiosampleFromSource, with the empty string for a null component. The grain is therefore one edge per release row: target, datasource and the source sample label, resolved to the two biosample ids. The release's own declared key is (celltypeBiosampleId, tissueBiosampleId, targetId, datasourceId) and is not unique: 83,290,030 rows carry 83,223,889 distinct 4-tuples. The binding's 7-part key gives 83,289,724, and the 306 remaining rows differ only in the measured quantiles.
Both biosample ids resolve exactly in biosample.biosampleId, so no separator normalisation is needed.
The edge points at the most specific biosample: celltypeBiosampleId when present, otherwise tissueBiosampleId.
Both ids are properties, because the cell type is a direct ontology child of the tissue in only 13 of 1,108 observed pairs, so a walk up the biosample hierarchy does not recover the tissue.
A baseline expression edge is a measured distribution in a biosample class from one source.
The four datasources measure different quantities.
A null specificity_score occurs on all 504,046 PRIDE rows: the source does not compute it.
164,481 rows carry no quantiles.
1,051,867 of the 82,116,120 measured triples carry measurements from two or three datasources in different units (CPM pseudobulk counts, TPM, iBAQ protein abundance).
1,101,388 triples carry more than one row in total.

Within gtex, 57,804 target-tissue pairs are two source labels mapped to one ontology term (Brain - Cerebellum and Brain - Cerebellar Hemisphere both UBERON_0002037), which is why the source labels are in the key rather than on the edge.
The release's field description swaps the two fromSource labels (it calls tissueBiosampleFromSource the cell type); the values are the source's own sample names for the field they sit in.
targetFromSourceId is non-null only on the 504,046 PRIDE rows and holds UniProt accessions, not Ensembl genes.

purpose.text: Read mechanismOfAction as the probe's mechanism labels.

limitations.text: Null means the source gives no mechanism label, not an unknown mechanism.
The labels are not a controlled vocabulary, are unordered and are not a pharmacological proof of action.

claims.text: The mechanism labels the probe source attaches to the probe.
One to three strings on 886 rows (796 with one, 88 with two, 2 with three); null on 379. Values are free text such as inhibitor, agonist, degrader or allosteric modulator.

purpose.text: Distinguish experimental from calculated probe assessments.

limitations.text: Origin qualifies the scores; it is not the molecule's development stage or the evidence type of a clinical claim.

claims.text: How the probe's assessment was obtained: experimental or calculated.
One value on 900 rows and two on 365; only experimental and calculated occur.

purpose.text: Read control to identify the probe's control compound or control note.

limitations.text: A null control means the source records no control, not that none exists.
A control name is not a MoleculeNode link and does not establish that the pair was assayed together.

claims.text: The control compound or control note recorded for the probe row.
Non-null on 210 rows. Values mix compound names (BI-6953, WEB2387) with notes such as 'No control'.
Null on 1,055 rows.

purpose.text: Filter probes by the source's high-quality flag.

limitations.text: It is the source's assessment, not a release grade, a potency threshold or a comparison across probe sources.

claims.text: The probe source's high-quality-probe flag.
True on 858 rows and false on 407; no nulls.

purpose.text: Compare probes by the Probes & Drugs druggability score.

limitations.text: The scale is the source's and is not normalised by the release; do not threshold it or compare it with isHighQuality as if they were the same quantity.

claims.text: The Probes & Drugs druggability score recorded for the probe.
A numeric score with no nulls or NaN in 26.09.

purpose.text: Compare probe activity in cells across probes.

limitations.text: Null and NaN both mean no score; the release writes NaN.
It carries no unit or assay context and is not comparable with scoreInOrganisms.
NaN is the source's missing marker, not a low score.

claims.text: The source's probe-activity score in cells.
NaN on 454 rows.

purpose.text: Compare probe activity in organisms across probes.

limitations.text: Null and NaN both mean no score; the release writes NaN.
It carries no species, dose or endpoint and is not comparable with scoreInCells.
NaN is the source's missing marker, not a low score.

claims.text: The source's probe-activity score in organisms.
NaN on 454 rows.

purpose.text: Read target -> molecule for the release's chemical probes.

limitations.text: Rows with no drugId emit no edge, since a MoleculeNode is a ChEMBL molecule. A null control is not 'no control'.

urls stay in the source. targetFromSourceId is the pre-resolution symbol or accession and is not carried; every targetId resolves to a TargetNode. NaN in scoreInCells and scoreInOrganisms is the source's missing marker, not a measured score. A probe annotation is a research-reagent classification, not an approved drug, a potency claim or clinical safety evidence.
A high-quality probe is not a drug candidate and is not evidence that the target is druggable in patients.

claims.text: A chemical probe for the target: a molecule that the probe source names as a tool compound or control, with the source's quality and activity assessments.

targetId|HAS_CHEMICAL_PROBE|drugId|drugFromSourceId: 1,199 edges for the 1,265 source rows. (targetId, drugId) has 1,263 distinct values; the two colliding pairs both have a null drugId, so drugFromSourceId is part of the key.

The edge points at the ChEMBL MoleculeNode named by drugId. drugFromSourceId is the probe source's own identifier (PD...), not a ChEMBL id. mechanismOfAction and origin are lists on the edge; isHighQuality is the source's flag.
A high-quality probe is a useful experimental reagent.
66 rows have no drugId because the probe is named only by the source id.
A null control occurs on 1,055 rows.
urls are 1 to 6 niceName/url structs per row.
NaN in scoreInCells and scoreInOrganisms occurs on 454 rows each.

purpose.text: Rank targets by constraint score within one family.

limitations.text: Not a probability that the gene is essential and not comparable across families.

claims.text: The release's constraint score for the target under this family.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
Higher means more constrained within this family's release scale.
Null for rows where the release did not compute a score.

purpose.text: Compare exp with obs.

claims.text: The expected number of variants under the release's null model.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
The pair underlies oe.
The null model and its covariates stay in the source dataset.
Null when the release did not compute an expectation.

purpose.text: Read obs with exp to derive the observed-to-expected ratio.

limitations.text: The cohort behind the count is not carried on the edge.

claims.text: The observed number of variants for the target under this family.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
An integer count, not a rate.
Null when the release did not report the count.

purpose.text: Read oe to identify depletion under this constraint family.

limitations.text: The ratio is not a significance test; use the release's score for its ranking.

claims.text: The observed-to-expected variant ratio.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
Values below one indicate depletion; the bounds are oeLower and oeUpper.
Null when obs or exp is missing.

purpose.text: Read together with oe and oeUpper.

claims.text: The lower bound of the confidence interval on oe.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
The interval's method and level stay in the source dataset.
Null when the release did not compute an interval.

purpose.text: Read together with oe and oeLower.

claims.text: The upper bound of the confidence interval on oe.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
The interval's method and level stay in the source dataset.
Null when the release did not compute an interval.

purpose.text: Locate a gene in the constraint distribution by rank.

limitations.text: Do not compare ranks across constraint families.

claims.text: The gene's rank in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
A rank, not a percentile; ties and direction are defined by the source.
Null when the release did not rank the gene.

purpose.text: Group genes by coarse constraint position.

limitations.text: The bin width is release-specific and not carried here.

claims.text: The gene's bin index in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
A coarse position derived from the rank.
Null when the release did not assign a bin.

purpose.text: Group genes by six-bin constraint position.

limitations.text: The bin boundaries are release-specific and not carried here.

claims.text: The gene's six-bin index in the release's constraint distribution.
A qualifier on the target-to-family edge.
A coarser variant of upperBin.
Null when the release did not assign the six-bin index.

purpose.text: Read target -> constraint type for the target's constraint metrics.

limitations.text: No edge means the release carries no metric for that family and target.
Constraint is a depletion signal over population variation. It does not establish essentiality, pathogenicity or a tissue-specific effect, and scores are not comparable across families.
A null metric is missing, not zero.

claims.text: The target's constraint metrics under one constraint family (missense, loss of function or synonymous).
target.id -> constraintType: key = target::HAS_CONSTRAINT::constraint_type::constraintType. A target has at most one row per family in the release.

obs and exp are observed and expected variant counts, oe the ratio with oeLower/oeUpper bounds, score the release's constraint score, and upperRank/upperBin/upperBin6 the gene's position in the distribution.

purpose.text: Read target -> cross reference for the target's external identifiers.

limitations.text: No edge means the release did not list that identifier for the target.
A listed identifier is not proof that the external record describes the same molecule, and the release does not verify the external record.

claims.text: The target's record lists the external identifier.
target.id -> source:identifier: key = target::HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE::source:identifier.
source is the external namespace: PDB, InterPro, Reactome, HGNC, DrugBank, ChEMBL or signalP. identifier is the accession as listed.

purpose.text: Read isEssential once per target as the target-level essentiality flag.

limitations.text: It is not the cell-line-specific call and its computation is not in this dataset. A false flag does not mean the target has no dependency in any line.

claims.text: The release's target-level essentiality flag, computed from the essentiality screens.
True for 1,822 of 18,464 targets and false for the rest; no nulls.
It is repeated on every screen edge of a target.

purpose.text: Compare dependency strength across screens by geneEffect.

limitations.text: It is not a p-value, effect size in physical units or a clinical endpoint. Compare screens only on the release's own scale; the build does not renormalise.

claims.text: The DepMap gene-effect score for the target in the cell line.
A continuous score; more negative means stronger dependency. The release's description treats values below -1 as dependencies. Non-null on all 22,171,776 screens.

purpose.text: Read expression as the target's expression in the cell line.

limitations.text: A null is a source gap, not zero expression.
The unit and normalisation are the source's, and the value is not comparable with baseline_expression without an explicit mapping.

claims.text: The target's expression level in the cell line.
A continuous expression value, non-null on 20,923,498 screens. It is the only field that distinguishes the repeated screens of one target-cell-line pair.
Null on 1,248,278 screens.

purpose.text: Read mutation as screen context for the cell line.

limitations.text: Null means the source states no mutation label, not a wild-type line.
The dataset does not name the mutated gene, so read the label as screen context, not as a property of the target or of the cell line's genome.

claims.text: The mutation label recorded for the screen.
Only two values occur: damaging (85,430 screens) and hotspot (1,478); null on the other 22,084,868 screens.

purpose.text: Read target -> cell line for the DepMap essentiality screen.

limitations.text: No edge means the release has no screen row for that target-cell-line pair. A null expression or mutation is a source gap, not a zero expression or a wild-type line.

isEssential is target-level and must not be read as the cell-line-specific call; the per-line evidence is geneEffect. diseaseCellLineId is not carried because CellLineNode has no property for it. A dependency is an in-vitro observation, not essentiality in a human tissue or a therapeutic window.
A target that is essential in DepMap is not necessarily essential in patients, and DepMap essentiality does not show that the target cannot be safely modulated.

claims.text: A DepMap CRISPR screen in one cell line, measuring how strongly the cell line depends on the target.

targetId|HAS_ESSENTIALITY_SCREEN|depmapId|expression: 22,171,776 edges. There are only 21,409,328 distinct target-cell-line pairs: 703,552 pairs occur twice and 29,448 three times, and the repeated rows differ only in expression, so the expression value completes the key.

geneEffect is the DepMap gene-effect score; more negative means a stronger dependency, and the release's description treats values below -1 as dependencies, a threshold this edge does not apply. expression is the target's expression in the line. mutation is the screen's mutation label where present. isEssential is a target-level flag, identical on every screen edge of a target.
This is the release's largest target annotation: 22,171,776 edges over only 1,208 cell lines.
isEssential is true for 1,822 targets and false for 16,642.
diseaseCellLineId is null on 9,354,641 screens and for 503 of the 1,208 lines.
A dependency measured in a cancer cell line is a model observation.

purpose.text: Resolve the annotation's cited source.

limitations.text: The release's go array never carries a null source.
A shared source does not make two annotations the same statement.

claims.text: The GO reference or PubMed identifier cited for the annotation.
One component of the edge key.
Values are GO_REF accessions or PMID identifiers for the cited source.

purpose.text: Filter annotations by evidence code.

limitations.text: The release's go array never carries a null evidence code.
IEA marks an inferred electronic annotation and is not equivalent to a manual assertion.

claims.text: The GO evidence code that states how the annotation was made.
One component of the edge key.
Observed codes include IEA, IDA, IMP, TAS, NAS and ISS; the code is not a score.

purpose.text: Filter annotations by GO namespace.

limitations.text: The release's go array never carries a null aspect.
Do not read the letter as the term's own namespace; it is the release's spelling, and the term's own namespace is on the GO term node.

claims.text: The GO namespace the term belongs to, as a one-letter code.
One component of the edge key.
P is biological process, F molecular function and C cellular component.

purpose.text: Resolve the annotation's protein or RNA product.

limitations.text: No null value occurs in this release; an annotation without a named product is not represented.
The product is not a target identifier and can be a non-protein RNA product.

claims.text: The protein or RNA product the annotation is attached to.
One component of the edge key; the release never carries a null geneProduct in target.go.
Values are UniProt accessions or RNAcentral URS identifiers.

purpose.text: Resolve the annotation's ECO evidence term.

limitations.text: Null means the release lists no ECO accession for the annotation.
The ECO term refines the evidence code; it is not a confidence score.
A null is most often a GO_REF annotation without an ECO mapping.

claims.text: The Evidence and Conclusion Ontology accession supporting the evidence code.
One component of the edge key; the empty string stands in for a null value, which occurs in about one percent of rows.
Values are ECO accessions such as ECO:0000256.

purpose.text: Read target -> GO term for the target's GO annotations.

limitations.text: No edge means the release does not list that annotation. A term can appear several times for one target with different evidence codes.
The annotation is an assertion by the cited source, not a result the release verified. Annotations to ancestor terms are not expanded: the edge names only the term the release lists.

claims.text: The target is annotated with the GO term by one cited source under one evidence code. The edge is the annotation record, not GO hierarchy.

target.id -> go.id, discriminated by (go.source, go.evidence, go.aspect, go.geneProduct, go.ecoId): key = target::HAS_GO_ANNOTATION::go.id::source::evidence::aspect::geneProduct::ecoId, with the empty string for a null ecoId; geneProduct is never null in the release.

aspect is the GO namespace letter: P biological process, F molecular function, C cellular component. evidence is the GO evidence code (IEA, IDA, IMP, ...); ecoId is the ECO accession behind it; source is the GO_REF or PMID cited; geneProduct is the protein or RNA product the annotation attaches to.

purpose.text: Read target -> hallmark for the target's hallmark statements.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no hallmark statement for the target; an empty hallmark struct produces no edge.
Neither attribute prose nor a cancer-hallmark label is a measured phenotype, and the release attaches no score to the statement.

claims.text: The target carries the hallmark statement.
target.id -> hallmark node key: target::HAS_HALLMARK::hallmark::kind::category::pmid[::impact]::description, with impact present only for a cancerHallmark record.
The statement fields sit on the node because one target can carry several statements for the same hallmark category. The edge asserts only that the target carries the statement.

purpose.text: Filter homologues by homology class.

limitations.text: The classes answer different questions: paralogues sit in one genome, orthologues across genomes, and many-to-many records a family-level correspondence with no one-to-one gene. Do not rank or pool the classes.

claims.text: The Ensembl compara classification of the pair.

Six values: other_paralog (human-only, 3,484,279), ortholog_one2one (168,810, the 12 non-human species), within_species_paralog (human-only, 67,968), ortholog_many2many, ortholog_one2many and gene_split (9). Every non-human edge is an ortholog class; every human-query edge is a paralog or gene_split class.

purpose.text: Filter cross-species orthologues by the source's confidence flag.

limitations.text: Null means the source states no confidence for this pair class, not low confidence.
It is a source flag on a pair, not a probability, a score or a comparison between pairs of different classes.
Null is exactly the human rows: the flag is only populated for cross-species orthologue pairs, so every human paralogue edge and all 9 gene_split edges carry null.

claims.text: The source's confidence flag for the pair, carried as the text the release writes: '1', '0' or null.
Casting the column to boolean without keeping null makes 93.1% of the rows indistinguishable from '0'.

purpose.text: Compare sequence identity from the target side.

limitations.text: Sequence identity is not functional equivalence, and the value is directional: the reverse edge carries the complement measurement.

claims.text: Percentage identity of the query gene (this target) to the homologue, on the source's 0-100 scale.
0-100 with no nulls; higher is closer. Measured 0.0-100.0 in 26.09.

purpose.text: Compare sequence identity from the homologue side.

limitations.text: Not the reverse edge's queryPercentageIdentity: that value belongs to a different row and a different alignment, so neither copy is redundant.

claims.text: Percentage identity of the homologue to the query gene, on the source's 0-100 scale.
0-100 with no nulls. It is the same pair as queryPercentageIdentity measured from the other sequence, so the two values differ on 3,323,472 rows and are equal on 493,768.

purpose.text: Read target -> homology gene for the target's homologues.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no compara pair between the target and that gene. That is a source gap, not evidence that the target has no homologue.
Both directions are kept because each row is the release's own query measurement and the identity values are not symmetric; counting edges double-counts pairs.
A non-human homologue is a gene record only.
A mouse or zebrafish homologue is not a target of this release; only human homology genes can be targets.

claims.text: One Ensembl compara homology pair: the target has the named homologue gene, with the pair class, the source's confidence flag and the two directional percentage identities.
targetId|HAS_HOMOLOGUE|speciesId|targetGeneId: 3,817,240 edges, one per source row, unique; 25,537 of the 78,733 targets have at least one edge (1-1,335 each, median 19).

homologyType is the pair class: other_paralog 3,484,279, ortholog_one2one 168,810, within_species_paralog 67,968, ortholog_many2many 57,952, ortholog_one2many 38,222, gene_split 9. queryPercentageIdentity measures targetId against targetGeneId; targetPercentageIdentity is the same pair measured from the homologue's side. The two differ on 3,323,472 rows and agree on 493,768. isHighConfidence is the source's text flag, not a boolean.
53,196 targets have no homology row at all.
Human pairs are stored twice, once per direction: 3,544,066 of the 3,552,256 human rows have a reverse row with the two identity values swapped, the same homologyType and the same flag.
The 1,772,033 undirected human pairs account for 3,544,066 edges.
8,190 human rows have no reverse: 8,181 name one of the 46 human gene ids that are absent from target.id and 9 are gene_split.
Only 20,864 of the 20,910 human gene ids are targets.
Each human paralogue pair is stored in both directions.
The number of HAS_HOMOLOGUE edges is neither the number of homologue genes nor the number of undirected pairs.

purpose.text: Read target -> mouse model for models of the target's phenotypes.

limitations.text: No edge means the release records no mouse model for that target's phenotype.

The edge records the release's model curation, not that the mouse phenotype reproduces a human phenotype, and not that the target is validated in a mouse. One model can be attached to several human targets when the orthology mapping is not one-to-one.
The mouse phenotype is not the human phenotype, and the model does not demonstrate the target's role in the human disease.

claims.text: A mouse model is recorded against one of this human target's phenotypes: the release maps the model's mouse gene to the human target and records an observed MP phenotype for the model.
A mouse model of a phenotype is model-organism evidence about the target's biology.
targetFromSourceId|HAS_MOUSE_MODEL|biologicalModels.id: 37,474 distinct target-model pairs over the 256,254 model entries. The model id is the node key; rows repeating a pair only add phenotypes.

targetFromSourceId is the human target: 11,869 distinct ENSG values and all of them resolve to a TargetNode. targetInModelEnsemblId is the mouse gene (11,467 ENSMUSG values) and targetInModelMgiId its MGI accession (11,467 values); neither is a human target id, so neither keys this edge. biologicalModels is an array: each element is one model, and 745 of the 256,254 elements have a null id and produce no edge.
745 of the 256,254 model entries carry a null model id and cannot be keyed.

purpose.text: Read target -> profile -> attributes.

limitations.text: No edge means no profile was computed; none occur in 26.09.
The edge states that the release computed a profile for the target. It does not rank targets or compare profiles across releases: the Target Engine's scores are recomputed each build.

claims.text: The target's prioritisation profile. The relation is 1:1 and total over the release's targets; all attributes are on the profile node.
targetId|HAS_PRIORITISATION_PROFILE|targetId: 78,733 edges, one per target.
The edge carries no property because the profile node key is the target id, so any attribute on the edge would be a target-level duplicate.

purpose.text: Read target -> protein for the target gene's protein identifiers.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no protein identifier for the gene.
The edge reports a listed mapping, not an experimentally confirmed protein product or a stoichiometric claim.

claims.text: The target gene maps to the protein identifier.
target.id -> source:identifier: key = target::HAS_PROTEIN_IDENTIFIER::source:identifier.
One edge per identifier; a gene can carry several, including retired UniProt accessions under uniprot_obsolete.

purpose.text: Read target -> observation.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no safety observation for the target; it is not evidence that the target is safe.
The edge repeats the source's association, not a causal adverse-effect finding, a clinical risk or a severity grade.
No safety event for a target means the release has no row, not that the target has no safety liability.
A target absent from target_safety_event is not evidence that the target is safe; the source did not assess it.

claims.text: The target is associated with a safety observation reported by one datasource.
targetId|HAS_SAFETY_EVENT|safety event key: 4,387 edges, one per source row and unique.
The observation node carries the event text, accession, datasource, citation and page.
954 targets have at least one observation; the other targets were not assessed here.

purpose.text: Read target -> synonym for the target's synonym strings.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no such synonym for the target.
The edge is a naming fact. It does not mean the label is approved, current or unique to this target.

claims.text: The target is known by the synonym under one synonym kind and source.
target.id -> (kind, source, label): key = target::HAS_SYNONYM::kind::source::label.
kind names the array the string came from; the same label in two kinds produces two edges.

purpose.text: Read value as the release's assessment for the bucket.

limitations.text: A null value would mean the source could not assess the bucket; none occur.
The boolean collapses whatever evidence the bucket summarises; it is not a quantity.

claims.text: The release's boolean outcome for the target and bucket.
True on 59,845 edges; false on 468,487. No value is null.

purpose.text: Read modality and category on the bucket node.

limitations.text: Every assessed target has all 28 buckets, so a missing edge is a build gap rather than a negative assessment.

false is an asserted negative, not missing data. true is a source assessment, not demonstrated druggability, validated chemical matter or a clinical result. Do not count true buckets as a score or rank targets on the total.
A true bucket records the release's assessment for that axis only.
A target with several true buckets is more tractable than one with fewer; the buckets are independent evidence axes, not points.

claims.text: The target's yes/no assessment for one tractability bucket.
targetId|HAS_TRACTABILITY|modality|category: 528,332 edges, one per target and bucket, unique.
value is the release's boolean for the axis: 59,845 true and 468,487 false.

purpose.text: Read target -> transcript.

limitations.text: A target with no edge has no transcript rows in the release.
The edge asserts annotation, not expression. A transcript with no proteinId is non-coding, and sharing a target does not make two transcripts functionally equivalent.

claims.text: The transcript is annotated as a product of the target gene.
(targetId, transcriptId). 644,292 edges; every targetId resolves to target.id and transcriptId is unique, so 0 keys duplicate.
Exactly one transcript per target is the Ensembl canonical transcript; the rest are alternatives.

purpose.text: Read target -> subcellular location for the target's localisation statements.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no localisation for the target.
The edge repeats a resource's statement; it is not a measurement made in this release and not a claim about every cell type.

claims.text: The target is reported at the subcellular location.

target.id -> (location, source, termSL, labelSL, targetModifier): key = target::LOCALISED_IN::subcellular_location::location::source::termSL::labelSL::targetModifier, with the empty string for a null component.
The statement is on the location node. A target can have several edges for the same location when sources or isoforms differ.

purpose.text: Group pathway memberships by top-level Reactome category.

limitations.text: The release's pathways array never carries a null topLevelTerm.
The category is a display grouping; it is not the pathway's parent in Reactome.

claims.text: The release's top-level Reactome category for the pathway.
A qualifier of the membership, not part of the edge key.
Examples are Signal Transduction, Immune System and Metabolism.

purpose.text: Read target -> Reactome pathway for the target's pathway membership.

limitations.text: No edge means the release lists no Reactome membership for the target.
Pathway membership is curation. It does not state that the target is active in a tissue, nor that the pathway mediates a disease.

claims.text: The target is a member of the Reactome pathway.
target.id -> pathways.pathwayId: key = target::PARTICIPATES_IN::pathwayId. pathwayId is unique per target in the release.
topLevelTerm is the release's broad Reactome category for the pathway, not a parent edge and not a target-disease assertion.

purpose.text: Use this edge to read the most severe consequence the release assigns to a variant.

limitations.text: No edge does not mean no consequence; it means the release did not assign a most severe one.

The summary discards which transcript carries the consequence and which target it affects; those are separate edges. Only 26 distinct terms occur, so the edge cannot distinguish severity within a term.

purpose.text: The disease_hpo relation fulfils the HAS_CROSS_REFERENCE use as the attribution that places a listed external identifier on one phenotype term: each release row names its term and contributes one edge per listed pair, keyed by the phenotype and the source:identifier pair. It records the release's own listing and not verification of the external record, and because the node type is shared, a matching identifier also joins terms from other domains.

limitations.text: A term with a null or empty dbXRefs array emits no edge.

claims.text: One edge per dbXRefs element; the source is the phenotype node key and the target the split identifier node key.
Both endpoints are composed from the same row; the edge carries no qualifier property.

purpose.text: The disease_hpo relation fulfils the HAS_OBSOLETE_TERM use as the attribution that keeps a retired accession reachable from the phenotype term that lists it: each release row names its term and contributes one edge per retired accession, keyed by the phenotype and the accession. It supplies the historical link only, with no successor or merge and no synonym relation, and the accessions resolve to obsolete-term nodes rather than to current phenotype terms.

limitations.text: A null or empty obsoleteTerms array emits no edge.

claims.text: One edge per element of disease_hpo.obsoleteTerms.
The target is obsolete_term_node_key(element), so it is an OBSOLETE_TERM key and not a PHENOTYPE key.

purpose.text: The disease_hpo relation fulfils the IS_A use as the direct subtype link between a phenotype term and each parent the release lists: each release row contributes one edge per parent, keyed by the child and parent accessions, and both endpoints are phenotype terms. It supplies direct parents only, so ancestry is a traversal, and subtype is not a licence to inherit every annotation of the parent.

limitations.text: A null parents array emits no edge.

claims.text: One edge per element of disease_hpo.parents, keyed phenotype::child::IS_A::parent.
The row's id is the child and the element the parent; both are used as written.
15 terms carry a null parents array.

purpose.text: The target_prioritisation relation fulfils the PRIORITISATION_PROFILE use as the release's computed feature summary for one target: each relation row is one node, keyed by the target id, and the relation covers the targets the release prioritised. The node supplies the release's encoded flags and scores as written, so it is a roll-up over the release's other layers rather than an independent assessment, and a null attribute is a feature the release did not compute rather than a negative value.

limitations.text: A null targetId cannot key the node; none occur. A missing profile would mean the target was not prioritised; none occur in 26.09.
The binding copies the release's encodings without converting them, so the reader must apply the per-property rules; no value is rescaled or re-signed.
Do not join the profile back to tractability, safety, probe or expression rows: it is the release's computed roll-up, not an independent assessment, evidence or a ranking produced by this graph.

claims.text: One PrioritisationProfileNode per row of target_prioritisation, keyed by the target.
target_prioritisation.targetId: 78,733 rows and 78,733 distinct ids, all resolving to a TargetNode, so the node is 1:1 with the target universe.

The integer flags are stored as integers, not booleans: null is the feature not being computed, and hasSafetyEvent and isCancerDriverGene encode true as -1 and never as 1. On the distribution columns -1 is a sentinel of unknown meaning, while on those two columns it is a measured present.

purpose.text: The target relation fulfils the PROTEIN use as a protein-record identifier the target gene maps to: each target row's proteinIds element supplies one protein node, keyed by source:identifier, and the relation covers every identifier the release lists. The same accession listed by several targets is one node, but the relation supplies no structure, isoform function or expression and does not resolve retired accessions.

limitations.text: A target with no protein element is a gene for which the release lists no protein identifier; it is not evidence that the gene encodes no protein.
A null source or identifier cannot key the node and drops the row; the release carries none.
A retired accession does not resolve to a current entry, and the binding creates no edge to a transcript.

claims.text: One ProteinNode per element of target.proteinIds.
Keyed source:identifier; the same accession listed for several targets yields one node with several inbound edges.
source and id are copied from the element and name the namespace and accession as written.

purpose.text: The literature_entity_lut relation fulfils the PUBLICATION use as the release's citable literature entry for papers its matcher grounded at least one entity in: each distinct mention pmid becomes one node, keyed by the release's literature key, and the relation covers the text-mined corpus rather than every paper the release cites. It supplies the pmid and its PMC deposit but no title, date or verification, so a cited publication with no grounded mention has no node.

limitations.text: The binding reads only literature_entity_lut; a PMID that other release tables cite but the LUT does not carry has no node.
A paper absent here is outside the release's text-mined corpus; that is not a claim that the paper does not exist.
literature_vector is keyed by word and category with no entity identifier, so no binding reads it into a publication node or edge.
A null pmid cannot key a node; the mapping mints no placeholder publication.

claims.text: The table's grain is (pmid, keywordId); the build's exact-duplicate collapse leaves one node per distinct pmid: 173,137,629 mention rows become 21,938,364 nodes.
The node carries pmid and pmcid only; the row's date and year are not properties because one key carries two dates.

purpose.text: The literature_entity_lut relation fulfils the MENTIONS_DISEASE use as the text-match attribution that places a disease-vocabulary term in one publication: each DS release row supplies one edge, keyed by the pmid and the grounded disease id, and relevance ranks the mention within its paper. It covers only identifiers the matcher grounded in the DS bucket, which also holds phenotype, anatomy, process and variable terms; it records a mention, not the paper's stance or an association.

limitations.text: The binding trusts the DS bucket and does not check keywordId against disease.id; an id outside that table would dangle.

claims.text: One edge per LUT row whose keywordType is DS, keyed pmid::MENTIONS_DISEASE::keywordId.
keywordId is used unchanged as the disease node key; relevance is copied from the row onto the edge.

purpose.text: The literature_entity_lut relation fulfils the MENTIONS_MOLECULE use as the text-match attribution that places a drug or chemical in one publication: each CD release row supplies one edge, keyed by the pmid and the grounded ChEMBL id, and relevance ranks the mention within its paper. It covers only ChEMBL-grounded chemicals, so a drug named by brand, code or salt form without a grounding has no edge, and a mention is not a claim that the paper studies it.

limitations.text: The binding trusts the CD bucket and does not check keywordId against drug_molecule; an id outside that table would dangle.

claims.text: One edge per LUT row whose keywordType is CD, keyed pmid::MENTIONS_MOLECULE::keywordId.
keywordId is used unchanged as the molecule node key; relevance is copied from the row onto the edge.

purpose.text: The literature_entity_lut relation fulfils the MENTIONS_TARGET use as the text-match attribution that places a gene or protein in one publication: each GP release row supplies one edge, keyed by the pmid and the grounded Ensembl id, and relevance ranks the mention within its paper. It covers only identifiers the matcher grounded, so a symbol it did not map is missed, and a mention is not the paper's finding or experimental evidence.

limitations.text: The binding trusts the GP bucket and does not check keywordId against target; an id outside that table would dangle.

claims.text: One edge per LUT row whose keywordType is GP, keyed pmid::MENTIONS_TARGET::keywordId.
keywordId is used unchanged as the target node key; relevance is copied from the row onto the edge.

purpose.text: The reactome relation fulfils the PATHWAY use as the release's joinable pathway identity: one release row is one pathway node, keyed by the R-HSA accession, and the relation covers the pathways the release's file publishes. It supplies the published label but no hierarchy, which is left to the IS_PART_OF edge, and an R-HSA-shaped accession named elsewhere in the release mints no pathway here.

limitations.text: No node means the release's pathway file carries no such accession: an R-HSA accession named by another dataset mints no pathway here.
The key is the accession alone; the binding resolves no pathway name and no other namespace to a node.

claims.text: One ReactomePathwayNode per row of reactome.
reactome.id, the R-HSA accession as written: 2,883 rows and 2,883 distinct keys; no id and no label is null.
The binding reads id and label only; ancestors, descendants, children and path stay unread in reactome.

purpose.text: The reactome relation fulfils the IS_PART_OF use as the direct containment link between a pathway and each parent it lists: each release row is the child and contributes one edge per parent, keyed by the two accessions, and every parent resolves to a pathway. It supplies direct child-to-parent links only; ancestors and descendants are closures this walk reproduces, path stays an ordered route in the source, and a root pathway carries no parent edge.

limitations.text: An empty parents array emits no edge: the 29 pathways that are release roots carry none, and the binding adds no parent for them.
The binding emits child -> parent only and reads no children array, so a parent-to-child walk must traverse IS_PART_OF in reverse.

claims.text: One PathwayIsPartOfEdge per element of reactome.parents.
child reactome.id|parent reactome.id: 2,899 edges with 2,899 distinct pairs.
The row is the child and the array element the direct parent; a pathway with up to six parents yields one edge per parent.
Every parent key names a reactome row, so no edge of this set dangles.

purpose.text: The enhancer_to_gene relation fulfils the REGULATORY_ELEMENT use as the release's element-gene-study prediction record: each release row is one E2G prediction for one interval, gene, biosample and study, and supplies one node keyed by the interval id, covering every prediction row. It answers with the interval's coordinates, type, score, distance to the TSS and study; it is a model prediction, not a measured enhancer-gene interaction, and the same genomic interval recurs once per study, so the id count is not a count of distinct elements.

limitations.text: The binding does not deduplicate across studies: each prediction row is keyed by intervalId, so a study's repeated rows collapse while an interval reported by two studies remains two nodes.

claims.text: One REGULATORY_ELEMENT node per row of enhancer_to_gene, keyed by intervalId.
enhancer_to_gene.intervalId is never null: 48,808,491 rows carry 48,806,245 distinct ids; the 2,246 rows that repeat an id are exact duplicates and collapse in the build.
resourceScore is written to the two array properties resourceScoreName and resourceScoreValue in the row's array order, so position pairs each component name with its value.

purpose.text: The enhancer_to_gene relation fulfils the ACTIVE_IN use as the biosample context of one prediction: each release row names the prediction's interval and biosample, and supplies one edge keyed by the interval id and the biosample id, covering every prediction row. It answers with the assay's tissue or cell-type context, not measured chromatin state in a sample; the release offers no finer sample identity than the biosample.

limitations.text: The binding copies no biosample label onto the edge; biosampleName stays in the source because the BIOSAMPLE node holds it.

claims.text: One ACTIVE_IN edge per prediction row, keyed intervalId|ACTIVE_IN|biosampleId.
biosampleId is never null; the binding emits 48,806,245 edges, 1:1 with the element node.
All 322 distinct biosampleId values resolve to a BiosampleNode, so no edge leaves a dangling endpoint.

purpose.text: The enhancer_to_gene relation fulfils the REGULATES use as the link from one prediction record to the gene it names: each release row states the interval's gene, and supplies one edge keyed by the interval id and the gene id, one edge per element node. It answers with the model's predicted gene target and nothing more; it is not a measured regulatory effect or a target-disease assertion, and one genomic interval can be predicted to regulate several genes through other records.

limitations.text: The binding assigns no property to the edge; score, distanceToTss and intervalType stay on the element node.

claims.text: One REGULATES edge per prediction row, keyed intervalId|REGULATES|geneId.
geneId is never null; the binding emits 48,806,245 edges, 1:1 with the element node.
All 20,088 distinct geneId values resolve to a TargetNode, so no edge leaves a dangling endpoint.

purpose.text: The enhancer_to_gene relation fulfils the SUPPORTED_BY use as the dataset citation behind a prediction: every release row names the same publication, and supplies one edge keyed by the interval id and the PMID, so every element record reaches that one paper. It answers with the dataset's citation, not the evidence for an individual element-gene link; the edge is constant across the dataset and adds no discrimination.

limitations.text: The edge is constant across the dataset and adds no discrimination; it records the citation, not per-element evidence.

claims.text: One SUPPORTED_BY edge per prediction row, keyed intervalId|SUPPORTED_BY|pmid.
pmid is 38014075 on every row, so the binding emits 48,806,245 edges to one publication.
pmid is never null or empty.
38014075 resolves to a PublicationNode, so the edge leaves no dangling endpoint.

purpose.text: The target_safety_event relation fulfils the SAFETY_EVENT use as one datasource's observation that a target is associated with an event: each relation row is one node, keyed by the target, event, datasource, accession and page, and the relation covers the observations the release publishes. The node carries the source's event wording, accession, citation and page, while the target, the effects and the tissues are carried by their edges, so the node records an observation and asserts nothing about causality, incidence, severity or dose response.

limitations.text: No node means the release records no such observation: a row without targetId, event or datasource cannot be keyed and emits none.

targetId is part of the key but is not a property, so two targets reported with the same event, datasource, eventId and url produce two nodes with identical properties; read the target from the incoming HAS_SAFETY_EVENT edge, never by matching properties.
A null eventId or url is a source gap, not an empty accession or a page.

claims.text: One SafetyEventNode per row of target_safety_event.
targetId|event|datasource|eventId|url, with the empty string where eventId or url is null: 4,387 rows and 4,387 distinct keys.
The binding copies event, eventId, datasource, literature and url from the row; eventId is carried as the source's accession and resolved to no node.
No row has a null targetId, event or datasource; eventId is null on 2,176 rows and url on 1,941.

purpose.text: The target_safety_event relation fulfils the HAS_EFFECT use as the statement that an observation reports a direction and dosing context: each relation row supplies an edge for each effects element it carries, keyed by the observation and the descriptor, covering the effect statements the release publishes. The relation supplies the source's descriptor pair and no rank between a row's elements, so it orders no effects and states no mechanism.

limitations.text: No edge means the observation states no effect: a null or empty effects array emits none.
direction|dosing is the whole descriptor: the binding carries no rank or index for the elements of one row, so two elements sharing the pair would not be distinguishable as edges.

claims.text: One HAS_EFFECT edge per effects element of a safety row.
safety event key|HAS_EFFECT|direction|dosing, with the empty string for a null: 2,349 edges, unique per observation and descriptor.
2,314 rows carry effects and 35 of them carry two; the 2,073 rows with a null effects array emit none.

purpose.text: The target_safety_event relation fulfils the OBSERVED_IN use as the tissue an observation was reported in: each relation row supplies an edge for each biosample element that names a tissue, keyed by the observation and the normalised tissue id, covering the tissue contexts the release records. The relation promotes the tissue id only, so a cell-only element contributes no edge, and the source's tissue label is not carried because the node supplies the vocabulary label.

limitations.text: No edge means the observation names no tissue: a row with no biosamples array, or an element with no tissueId, emits no edge.
The key rewrites a tissue id written with a colon (UBERON:...) to the underscore form of the node key, so an id taken from another source must be rewritten the same way or the edge is missed.

claims.text: One OBSERVED_IN edge per non-null tissueId in a biosamples element.
safety event key|OBSERVED_IN|tissueId: 5,072 edges over the 2,601 observations that name a tissue, unique per observation and tissue. 31 elements are written with a colon.
An observation names up to six tissues. The binding promotes tissueId only: cellId is null on all 5,599 elements, and cellLabel, cellFormat and the source tissueLabel stay in the source.
438 biosamples elements are cell-only and 1,786 rows carry no biosamples array.

purpose.text: The target_safety_event relation fulfils the SAFETY_EVENT_EFFECT use as the direction and dosing context a safety observation reports: each distinct descriptor in the relation's effect elements is one node, keyed by the direction and dosing pair, and the relation supplies the descriptors its observations report. The node is a shared vocabulary entry with no identity beyond the pair, and the HAS_EFFECT edge, not the node, ties it to an observation, so a null dosing records a source gap rather than a no-dose context.

limitations.text: A row with a null or empty effects array emits no effect record.
The empty-string dosing component in the key stands for a null dosing, not for a reported no-dose context.
The node set is a closed vocabulary, not an entity set; the HAS_EFFECT edge, not the node, ties a descriptor to an observation.

claims.text: One SafetyEventEffectNode per distinct effects element; 9 nodes from 2,349 array elements.
Keyed direction|dosing, with the empty string for a null dosing.
direction and dosing are copied from the element; direction is the signed statement and dosing is the context label.

purpose.text: The so relation fulfils the SO_TERM use as the release's consequence-class identity: one release row is one term node, keyed by the SO accession in colon form, and the relation covers the release's sequence-ontology subset. It supplies the class label but no severity or impact, and the release's consequence columns use the underscore spelling, so a consumer must convert the separator before matching.

limitations.text: A term absent from so is outside the release's SO subset.
The node carries no severity or impact; those are properties of the specific consequence edge.
Do not join the consequence columns as written: they carry the underscore form of the identifier, so convert the separator to a colon before matching so.id.

claims.text: One SOTermNode per row of so.
Keyed so.id; 2,620 rows and 2,620 distinct SO: accessions, with no null id or label.
label is copied from the row; the node denotes a consequence class.

purpose.text: The study relation fulfils the STUDY use as the unit a consumer weighs a piece of evidence by, through its design, cohort size and publication: each relation row is one node, keyed by the study id, and the relation covers the studies the release publishes. The row supplies the design, cohort counts, trait wording and publication metadata, while the disease, target, biosample, publication and credible sets are carried by their edges, so the node qualifies evidence without recording an outcome and is not the same unit as a publication.

limitations.text: A row with a null studyId cannot key a node and is dropped.
Do not aggregate the resulting nodes by publication or by trait without stating the unit; one publication and one trait each cover several study rows.

claims.text: One STUDY node per study row; the mapping applies no filter on studyType or on missing metadata.
publicationTitle, publicationFirstAuthor, publicationDate and publicationJournal are copied from the study row onto the node.

purpose.text: The credible_set relation fulfils the HAS_CREDIBLE_SET use as the ownership that places a fine-mapped set under the study that produced it: each relation row supplies one edge, keyed by the study id and the study-locus id, and the relation covers every set that names its study. The relation is read from the credible-set side, so a study with no fine-mapped locus contributes no edge, and the edge asserts membership of the set without claiming that the study's trait is caused by any variant in it.

limitations.text: A row with a null studyId or studyLocusId emits no edge; no placeholder endpoint is minted.
The mapping reads credible_set, not study, so a study with no credible-set row has no edge.

claims.text: One edge per row of credible_set, keyed studyId::HAS_CREDIBLE_SET::studyLocusId.
Source and target are the row's studyId and studyLocusId, used as written.

purpose.text: The study relation fulfils the MEASURED_IN use as the experimental setting that locates a molecular-QTL measurement: each relation row supplies an edge where it names a biosample, keyed by the study id and the biosample id, and the relation covers every QTL study that carries one. The relation leaves a GWAS study with no edge because it has no molecular assay context, and the edge is coarse: it places a measurement in a biosample without saying the target is expressed there in every condition.

limitations.text: A null biosampleId is dropped; no placeholder biosample is minted.

claims.text: One edge per study row with a non-null biosampleId, keyed studyId::MEASURED_IN::biosampleId.
The target is the row's biosampleId used as written; the binding performs no biosample lookup.

purpose.text: The study relation fulfils the MEASURES_TARGET use as the gene whose molecular trait a QTL study measures: each relation row supplies an edge where it names a gene, keyed by the study id and the gene id, and the relation covers every QTL study that carries one. The relation leaves a GWAS study with no edge because it measures a trait rather than a gene, and the edge names the measured gene without asserting a target-disease association or a drug-target claim.

limitations.text: A null geneId is dropped; no placeholder target is minted.

claims.text: One edge per study row with a non-null geneId, keyed studyId::MEASURES_TARGET::geneId.
The target is the row's geneId used as written; the binding performs no gene lookup.

purpose.text: The study relation fulfils the PUBLISHED_AS use as the citation that traces a study record to the publication it cites: each relation row supplies an edge where it carries a PubMed reference, keyed by the study id and the PMID, and the relation covers every study that cites a paper. The relation supplies the study's own reference, so several studies can share one publication, and a PMID outside the release's publication set leaves an edge on no node.

limitations.text: A null pubmedId is dropped; no stand-in publication is minted.

claims.text: One edge per study row with a non-null pubmedId, keyed studyId::PUBLISHED_AS::pmid.
The target is the study's pubmedId used verbatim; the binding does not look it up in literature_entity_lut.

purpose.text: The study relation fulfils the STUDIES_DISEASE use as the trait a study is filed under in the release: each relation row supplies an edge for each mapped trait term it carries, keyed by the study id and the disease id, and the relation covers the annotated studies. The relation supplies the release's mapping of the source trait rather than a diagnosis, and a molecular-QTL study contributes no edge, which is the release's shape and not an uncurated trait.

limitations.text: An empty or null diseaseIds array emits no edge; the binding does not fall back to traitFromSource.

claims.text: One edge per element of study.diseaseIds, keyed studyId::STUDIES_DISEASE::diseaseId.
The mapped id is used as written; the binding does not map traitFromSource itself.

purpose.text: The target relation fulfils the SUBCELLULAR_LOCATION use as a localisation statement reported for a target: each target row's subcellularLocations element supplies one statement node, keyed by location, source, term, label and modifier, and the relation covers every statement the release lists. It supplies a reported observation, not a measurement, and the free-text location can carry qualifiers that termSL does not capture.

limitations.text: The release never carries a null location or source; a null termSL, labelSL or targetModifier is encoded as the empty string in the key but stays null as a property.
The node is a statement record, not an ontology term; termSL is the only normalized handle.

claims.text: One SubcellularLocationNode per element of target.subcellularLocations.
Keyed subcellular_location::location::source::termSL::labelSL::targetModifier, with the empty string for a null component.
location, source, termSL, labelSL and targetModifier are copied from the element; a different source or isoform is a different node.

purpose.text: The target relation fulfils the SYNONYM use as the naming fact that lets a consumer match an alternative target name within one kind and source: each distinct general-synonym element of the relation is one node, keyed by the kind, source and label, and the relation supplies the general synonyms its targets list. The node carries the general-synonym kind because only the relation's synonyms array supplies it, and the same string under another kind or source stays a separate node, so the node is a vocabulary entry rather than an approval, a current status or an identity for one target.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no general synonym for the target.
A synonym is a naming fact, not an approval, current status or a uniqueness claim.

claims.text: One SynonymNode per element of target.synonyms.
Keyed synonym::synonym::source::label; the same string in another kind is a different node, and a label shared by two targets with the same source is one node with two inbound edges.
kind is the literal 'synonym' because the string came from the general synonym array, not from symbolSynonyms or nameSynonyms.
label and source are copied from the element.

purpose.text: The target relation fulfils the SYNONYM use as the naming fact that lets a consumer match an alternative target symbol within one kind and source: each distinct symbol-synonym element of the relation is one node, keyed by the kind, source and label, and the relation supplies the alternative symbols its targets list. The node carries the symbol-synonym kind because only the relation's symbolSynonyms array supplies it, and the same string under another kind or source stays a separate node, so the node is a vocabulary entry rather than an approval or an identity for one target.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no alternative symbol for the target.
An alternative symbol is not the approvedSymbol property; a synonym is a naming fact, not an approval or uniqueness claim.

claims.text: One SynonymNode per element of target.symbolSynonyms.
Keyed synonym::symbolSynonym::source::label; the same string in another kind is a different node, and a label shared by two targets with the same source is one node with two inbound edges.
kind is the literal 'symbolSynonym' because the string came from target.symbolSynonyms, not from synonyms or nameSynonyms.
label and source are copied from the element.

purpose.text: The target relation fulfils the SYNONYM use as the naming fact that lets a consumer match an alternative target name within one kind and source: each distinct name-synonym element of the relation is one node, keyed by the kind, source and label, and the relation supplies the alternative names its targets list. The node carries the name-synonym kind because only the relation's nameSynonyms array supplies it, and the same string under another kind or source stays a separate node, so the node is a vocabulary entry rather than an approval or an identity for one target.

limitations.text: No element means the release lists no alternative name for the target.
An alternative name is not the approvedName property; a synonym is a naming fact, not an approval or uniqueness claim.

claims.text: One SynonymNode per element of target.nameSynonyms.
Keyed synonym::nameSynonym::source::label; the same string in another kind is a different node, and a label shared by two targets with the same source is one node with two inbound edges.
kind is the literal 'nameSynonym' because the string came from target.nameSynonyms, not from synonyms or symbolSynonyms.
label and source are copied from the element.

purpose.text: The target relation fulfils the TARGET use as the release's joinable target identity: each target row is one gene-level node, keyed by the Ensembl gene id, and the relation covers the release's target universe. It supplies the released symbol, name, biotype, function text and genomic span, but no protein isoform or transcript, so those readings stay outside the gene-level record. The relation's membership is the release's target set, not every human gene, and a null symbol is a release gap.

limitations.text: A row with a null id cannot be keyed and is dropped. The release's target rows otherwise have an id.
A TargetNode is not a protein structure, a transcript or a complex. Do not read a gene-level property as an isoform-specific fact.

claims.text: The node carries the gene-level annotation. Protein, transcript, pathway, ontology and cross-reference facts are separate edges.
One TargetNode per row of target, keyed by the Ensembl gene id.
target.id

purpose.text: The association_overall_direct relation fulfils the ASSOCIATED_WITH use as the release's direct target-disease aggregate: each row is one target-disease pair, keyed by the target and disease ids, and the relation covers every pair for which direct evidence was folded. It supplies the weighted direct score, the evidence-row count and the recent-growth signal for that pair, but it does not roll evidence through the disease ontology and does not rank or explain the association.

limitations.text: No row means no direct aggregate for the pair; it is not a measured zero association.
The yearly timeseries is not carried on the edge; use currentNovelty only as a recent-growth signal. The score is not causal.

claims.text: The score is a weighted aggregate over direct evidence. Evidence count counts contributing evidence rows, not independent studies.
One edge per target-disease pair in association_overall_direct, carrying the release's direct aggregate.
The (targetId, diseaseId) pair; aggregationValue is constant 'None'.

purpose.text: The association_by_datasource_direct relation fulfils the ASSOCIATED_WITH_BY_DATASOURCE_DIRECT use as the attribution of a direct target-disease association to one datasource: each row is one target, disease and datasource combination, keyed by those ids, and the relation covers every source that contributed a direct aggregate to the pair. It supplies that source's own fold, not a share of the overall score, and it does not carry the timeseries or a cross-source comparison.

limitations.text: A null targetId, diseaseId or aggregationValue would drop the row; the release carries none. No edge means the datasource reported no direct aggregate for the pair, not a measured zero.
Per-source scores are not shares of the overall score and are not comparable across datasources. The timeseries array is not carried on the edge; currentNovelty is the only temporal signal here.

claims.text: 7,225,847 pairs produce 1 to 13 edges each. Every edge stores aggregationValue as a categorical id, not a score. The pair set is the same as association_overall_direct, so this layer partitions the overall report.

purpose.text: The variant relation fulfils the HAS_MOST_SEVERE_CONSEQUENCE use as the release's most severe SO consequence for a variant: each variant row with an assigned consequence supplies one edge, keyed by the variant and the normalized SO term, and the relation covers every variant that has an assigned consequence. It is a per-variant summary that discards the transcript and target carrying the consequence, and a missing edge means no consequence was assigned, not that none exists.

limitations.text: No edge for a variant whose mostSevereConsequenceId is null, not a variant with no consequence.
Only the SO vocabulary's id form is normalized; the term labels and severity ranking are the release's.
The edge is variant-level and does not name a transcript or target.

claims.text: One edge per variant with a non-null mostSevereConsequenceId, pointing at the normalized SO term.
variantId -> so.id after replacing SO_ with SO: in the consequence id.
7,886,761 edges; the one variant with a null id is filtered by drop_null.
The rewrite is measured: all 26 distinct consequence ids fail to join so.id as written and all 26 resolve after it.

purpose.text: The variant relation fulfils the HAS_PREDICTED_EFFECT_ON use as one method's predicted effect of a variant on a target: each variantEffect element that names a target supplies one edge, keyed by the variant, target and method, and the relation covers every target-bearing element. It supplies method-specific predictions, not a consensus or an experimental effect, and elements without a target have no target endpoint.

limitations.text: No edge means the element names no target or the variant has no variantEffect element; it does not mean the variant is neutral for the target.
Each method is a separate edge; there is no consensus edge. Scores are method-specific.
VEP and FoldX predictions stay in the source with no target endpoint.

claims.text: One edge per variantEffect array element that names a target, keyed by variant, target and method.
(variantId, targetId, method). assessment is omitted from the key because it is null on every GERP row and adds no discrimination: 0 duplicate triples and 0 duplicate four-tuples.
9,423,729 of 17,960,867 elements become edges.
The 8,537,138 elements without a target are VEP (7,886,762) and FoldX (650,376) and are filtered by drop_null.
Every targetId resolves to target.id (0 dangling of 76,496 distinct targets).

purpose.text: The variant relation fulfils the HAS_TRANSCRIPT_CONSEQUENCE use as one predicted protein-altering consequence of a variant on a transcript: each HIGH- or MODERATE-impact transcriptConsequences element supplies one edge, keyed by the variant and transcript ids, and the relation covers that published subset. It omits LOW and MODIFIER elements, so a missing edge is not a neutral consequence, and the prediction is not an observed effect.

limitations.text: No edge therefore means the consequence is not protein-altering at HIGH or MODERATE level, not that the variant has no transcript consequence.
siftPrediction and polyphenPrediction are null on every element, so the published edges carry no SIFT or PolyPhen value.

claims.text: One edge per variant transcript consequence whose impact is HIGH or MODERATE, pointing at the transcript node.
(variantId, transcriptId). 0 duplicate pairs in the published subset; the full source array has 280,906,222 elements and 0 duplicate pairs.
1,431,373 edges: HIGH 296,862 and MODERATE 1,134,511.
Every transcriptId resolves to transcript.transcriptId and every targetId to target.id (0 dangling). All source elements have both ids.
This is a bounded subset of a 280.9M-element array: carrying all elements would add 279,474,849 mostly intronic/intergenic rows.
LOW (667,184) and MODIFIER (278,807,665) transcript-consequence elements are not published.
